● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · Suppliers retry, so an older update (updatedAtUtc earlier than the stored
     one) can arrive after a newer one. The spec doesn't cover this. What 
     should happen? → Ignore stale, report it (Recommended)
     · For the 100 requests per rolling 60s per supplier: should rejected 
     (throttled) requests count toward the window, and where should the limiter 
     state live? → Rejected don't count; in-memory (but mention in readme thet 
     for production application it shuld be in aouter storage)
     · What should 'ingested' mean in the stats, and what should the stats 
     endpoint return for a supplier that has never sent anything? → Ingested = 
     created + updated; unknown supplier gets zeros (Recommended)
     · How should the ingest endpoint signal each outcome? Throttled will be 429
     with a Retry-After header, and invalid payloads will be 400 
     ProblemDetails. → 201 created / 200 updated / 200 duplicate (Recommended)

     │ - SlidingWindowRateLimiter (singleton): ConcurrentDictionary<string,    │
     │   Window>. Each window holds a Queue<DateTimeOffset> guarded by a lock. │
     │   - On each call: dequeue timestamps <= now - 60s. If count >= limit,   │
     │     reject with RetryAfter = oldest + 60s - now. Otherwise enqueue now  │

     │   - Rejected calls enqueue nothing (per your decision).                 │

● I'll update the plan with your changes. Here are my answers to your two
  questions.

  Supplier identity: (supplierId, reservationId) or reservationId alone?
  - The spec says "the same reservationId arrives again", which can be read as
    reservationId alone being the key. But every payload carries a supplierId,
    and the stats and throttling are per supplier, so the data model is clearly
    supplier-scoped.
  - With reservationId alone, supplier B could overwrite supplier A's
    reservation just by reusing an id. Ids like "1001" are issued by each
    supplier independently, so collisions are realistic. That's a silent
    data-corruption path. It also muddies the stats: whose "ingested" count does
    the overwrite belong to?
  - I recommend the composite key. A reservation is identified by who sent it
    plus their id, so two suppliers never touch each other's records. The README
    should state this as an assumption.
  - A third option is to key on reservationId alone and reject a different
    supplier with 409. It follows the literal spec and is still safe, but it
    adds an outcome, a test and a rule the spec never asked for, and one
    supplier's id choices could then block another supplier. I don't think it's
    worth it here.

  Order of checks: validate, then throttle, then ingest
  - Throttling has to come before any DB access, because the limiter exists to
    protect the DB and the service from heavy suppliers.
  - Validation comes first because the limiter keys on supplierId. A body that
    fails validation (missing or empty supplierId) can't be attributed to
    anyone, so it can't be throttled, and it never reaches the DB anyway.
  - The cost is that a supplier flooding invalid requests is never throttled. I
    think that's acceptable, since those requests cost almost nothing (no DB, no
    state). It's a real tradeoff, so it goes in the README.
  - Throttle-first would count every request, as the spec literally says. It
    would need a separate step that extracts supplierId from the raw body before
    validation, which is more code for a marginal gain. I'm keeping
    validate-first. Tell me if you'd rather have throttle-first.

  Now the plan edits.

     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │               │ {ingested:0, throttled:0}.                            │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├───────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │               │ 201 Created (no Location header), 200 Updated, 200    │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │ Responses     │ Duplicate, 200 Stale. Every success body has an       │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │               │ explicit status. 429 + Retry-After for throttled. 400 │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │               │ ProblemDetails for invalid input.                     │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├───────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │ Test          │ NUnit                                                 │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │ framework     │                                                       │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├───────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │ Reservation   │ Composite (supplierId, reservationId), see below.     │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │ identity      │                                                       │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ └───────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┘                                                                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Why the composite key                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The spec's "same reservationId" could be read as reservationId alone.   │
     │ But ids are issued by each supplier independently, so collisions across │
     │ suppliers are realistic. Keying on reservationId alone would let        │
     │ supplier B silently overwrite supplier A's record and muddy             │
     │ per-supplier stats. A reservation is therefore identified by who sent   │
     │ it plus their id. The alternative (global key plus a 409 when the       │
     │ supplier differs) was rejected as extra rules the spec never asked for. │
     │ This goes in the README.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ My assumptions (to list in the README)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Identity is (supplierId, reservationId). Different suppliers may      │
     │   reuse the same reservation id, and cannot update each other's         │
     │   records.                                                              │
     │ - "Same details" means roomId, checkIn, checkOut, price and             │
     │   updatedAtUtc are all equal. Equal updatedAtUtc with other fields      │
     │   different is treated as an Update (the spec says different details    │
     │   means update).                                                        │
     │ - Order of checks is validate, then throttle, then ingest.              │
     │   - Throttle must precede all DB access, since its purpose is to        │
     │     protect the DB.                                                     │
     │   - Validate must precede throttle because the limiter keys on          │
     │     supplierId, which an invalid body may not have.                     │
     │   - Tradeoff: a supplier flooding invalid requests is not throttled.    │
     │     Those requests are cheap (no DB, no state), so this is accepted and │
     │     documented.                                                         │
     │ - Supplier ids are matched exactly (case-sensitive, trimmed).           │
     │ - Validation rules: required non-empty strings, checkOut strictly after │
     │   checkIn (equal values are rejected), price >= 0.                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Target structure                                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Single API project with folders (a four-project Clean Architecture      │
     │ would be over-engineering here), plus one test project.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ ReservationsHandler.sln                                                 │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api/                                                │
     │   Program.cs                      composition root only (extension      │
     │ methods for DI)                                                         │
     │   Controllers/ReservationsController.cs   thin: maps outcome -> HTTP    │
     │   Contracts/                      IngestReservationRequest,             │
     │ IngestReservationResponse, SupplierStatsResponse                        │
     │   Domain/                         Reservation (record), IngestStatus    │
     │ enum                                                                    │
     │   Services/                       IReservationIngestionService + impl   │
     │ (orchestration)                                                         │
     │   RateLimiting/                   ISupplierRateLimiter,                 │
     │ SlidingWindowRateLimiter, RateLimitOptions                              │
     │   Data/                           ISqliteConnectionFactory,             │
     │ DatabaseInitializer, DapperTypeHandlers,                                │
     │                                   IReservationRepository + impl,        │
     │ ISupplierStatsRepository + impl                                         │
     │   Infrastructure/                 GlobalExceptionHandler                │
     │ (IExceptionHandler -> ProblemDetails)                                   │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api.Tests/    NUnit                                 │
     │ README.md                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step-by-step                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 1. Scaffold and packages                                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Delete the weather sample from Program.cs. Keep Swagger in            │
     │   Development.                                                          │
     │ - Add packages: Dapper, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.                          │
     │ - Create the NUnit test project (dotnet new nunit) with NUnit,          │
     │   NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk,                            │
     │   Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing,                                     │
     │   Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing. Reference the API project  │
     │   and add it to the .sln.                                               │
     │ - Add public partial class Program; so WebApplicationFactory can see    │
     │   it.                                                                   │
     │ - Why: a clean baseline before any logic. TimeProvider.Testing lets us  │
     │   test the 60s window without sleeping.                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 2. Domain and contracts                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Reservation as an immutable record (SupplierId, ReservationId,        │
     │   RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut, Price (decimal), UpdatedAtUtc, plus a      │
     │   SameDetailsAs(other) method).                                         │
     │ - IngestStatus { Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale, Throttled }.       │
     │ - Request DTO with DataAnnotations plus IValidatableObject for checkOut │
     │   > checkIn. [ApiController] then gives automatic 400 ProblemDetails.   │
     │ - Use DateTimeOffset and normalize to UTC at the boundary. Use decimal  │
     │   for money.                                                            │
     │ - Why: keeps the HTTP contract separate from the domain and avoids a    │
     │   validation library for 4 rules.                                       │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 3. Data layer (Dapper and SQLite)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISqliteConnectionFactory reads the connection string from config      │
     │   (Data Source=reservations.db). Tests override it with a temp file.    │
     │ - DatabaseInitializer runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS at startup:       │
     │   - Reservations(SupplierId, ReservationId, RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut,  │
     │     Price, UpdatedAtUtc, PRIMARY KEY (SupplierId, ReservationId))       │
     │   - SupplierStats(SupplierId PRIMARY KEY, Ingested INTEGER, Throttled   │
     │     INTEGER)                                                            │
     │ - Dapper type handlers: DateTimeOffset stored as ISO-8601 UTC text      │
     │   (sortable and comparable). decimal stored as TEXT to avoid REAL float │
     │   drift. Verify round-trips with a test.                                │
     │ - IReservationRepository.UpsertAsync(reservation) runs in one write     │
     │   transaction:                                                          │
     │   a. SELECT the existing row by key.                                    │
     │   b. None: INSERT, giving Created.                                      │
     │   c. Identical: nothing is written, giving Duplicate.                   │
     │   d. Incoming updatedAtUtc is older: nothing is written, giving Stale.  │
     │   e. Otherwise UPDATE, giving Updated.                                  │
     │   f. For Created and Updated, increment SupplierStats.Ingested in the   │
     │      same transaction (atomic upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE  │
     │      SET Ingested = Ingested + 1).                                      │
     │ - ISupplierStatsRepository: IncrementThrottledAsync, GetAsync (zeros if │
     │   no row).                                                              │
     │ - Concurrency: the SELECT-then-write must not race (two identical       │
     │   concurrent requests must yield exactly one Created). Use an immediate │
     │   (write-locking) transaction. Confirm that Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's     │
     │   chosen isolation level really takes the write lock up front, and      │
     │   prove it with the concurrency test in Step 7. If it doesn't, fall     │
     │   back to a per-key SemaphoreSlim.                                      │
     │ - Also enable PRAGMA busy_timeout so concurrent writers wait instead of │
     │   throwing "database is locked".                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 4. Rate limiter (the interesting part)                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISupplierRateLimiter.TryAcquire(supplierId) ->                        │
     │   RateLimitResult(Allowed, RetryAfter).                                 │
     │ - SlidingWindowRateLimiter implements the sliding window log algorithm  │
     │   (singleton): one log of accepted-request timestamps per supplier.     │
     │   ConcurrentDictionary<string, Window>, where each window holds a       │
     │   Queue<DateTimeOffset> (the log, in chronological order) guarded by a  │
     │   lock.                                                                 │
     │   - On each call: dequeue timestamps <= now - 60s. If count >= limit,   │
     │     reject with RetryAfter = oldest + 60s - now. Otherwise enqueue now  │
     │     and allow.                                                          │
     │   - Rejected calls enqueue nothing (per your decision).                 │
     │ - RateLimitOptions (limit = 100, window = 60s) bound via IOptions, so   │
     │   tests can use small values if needed.                                 │
     │ - Inject TimeProvider (built into .NET 8) instead of calling            │
     │   DateTime.UtcNow.                                                      │
     │ - Why a sliding log over a fixed window: the spec says "any rolling     │
     │   60-second window". A fixed window allows 200 requests across a        │
     │   boundary. Memory is bounded at 100 timestamps per supplier.           │
     │ - Known limitation (README): in-memory state is lost on restart and not │
     │   shared across instances. Idle windows are never evicted, which is     │
     │   fine at this scale.                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 5. Ingestion service                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ IReservationIngestionService.IngestAsync(Reservation) orchestrates:     │
     │ 1. limiter.TryAcquire(supplierId). If denied,                           │
     │    stats.IncrementThrottledAsync, then return Throttled(retryAfter).    │
     │ 2. Otherwise reservationRepo.UpsertAsync and return the outcome.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ It returns a small result type (status plus optional RetryAfter), not   │
     │ exceptions. Exceptions are for exceptional cases only. Why this layer:  │
     │ the controller stays trivial and the logic is unit-testable with fakes. │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 6. Controller and error handling                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest maps the outcome:                       │
     │   - Created: 201 with a body and no Location header (use                │
     │     StatusCode(201, body), not CreatedAtAction).                        │
     │   - Updated, Duplicate, Stale: 200.                                     │
     │   - Throttled: 429 with a Retry-After header and ProblemDetails.        │
     │   - Body: { status, supplierId, reservationId }.                        │
     │ - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId} returns { supplierId,        │
     │   ingested, throttled }.                                                │
     │ - GlobalExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, .NET 8) turns unexpected   │
     │   errors into a 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace leaked. Log the  │
     │   exception.                                                            │
     │ - Register everything in Program.cs through small AddXxx extension      │
     │   methods. Add CancellationToken through the stack.                     │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 7. Tests (the grader's confidence signal)                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ All tests are NUnit: [TestFixture], [SetUp]/[TearDown] for a fresh temp │
     │ DB per test, [TestCase] for validation variants, Assert.That(...,       │
     │ Is...) constraints. Concurrency tests use Task.WhenAll. Don't mark      │
     │ fixtures that share a DB or WebApplicationFactory as [Parallelizable].  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Unit, rate limiter (FakeTimeProvider):                                  │
     │ - 100 calls allowed, 101st rejected with a sensible RetryAfter.         │
     │ - After advancing 60s the supplier is allowed again, and the window is  │
     │   truly rolling (requests at t=0 and t=30 expire independently).        │
     │ - Suppliers are isolated from each other.                               │
     │ - Rejected calls don't extend the window.                               │
     │ - Concurrency: 300 parallel calls produce exactly 100 allowed.          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Integration (WebApplicationFactory with a temp-file SQLite DB per test  │
     │ class):                                                                 │
     │ - Created (201), then identical resend (200 Duplicate, with proof no    │
     │   write happened, e.g. ingested stat unchanged and the row unchanged),  │
     │   then changed price (200 Updated, row updated), then older             │
     │   updatedAtUtc (Stale, row unchanged).                                  │
     │ - Same reservationId from two different suppliers gives two independent │
     │   rows (one can't overwrite the other).                                 │
     │ - Concurrency: N parallel identical ingests produce exactly 1 Created,  │
     │   N-1 Duplicate, and ingested == 1.                                     │
     │ - 101st request from a supplier gets 429 with Retry-After. Another      │
     │   supplier is unaffected. Stats show ingested=100, throttled=1.         │
     │ - Validation: missing fields, checkOut == checkIn, checkOut < checkIn   │
     │   and negative price each return 400. checkOut one tick after checkIn   │
     │   is accepted.                                                          │
     │ - 201 response has no Location header.                                  │
     │ - Stats for an unknown supplier return zeros.                           │
     │ - Decimal and date round-trip fidelity through SQLite.                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 8. README (half a page, as the assignment requires)                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Three sections:                                                         │
     │ 1. Assumptions: the list above, with reasons.                           │
     │ 2. Claude suggestions I disagreed with or changed: fill this in         │
     │    honestly during the session.                                         │
     │ 3. With more time: distributed limiter (Redis), migrations              │
     │    (DbUp/FluentMigrator), idempotency/outbox, auth, metrics, eviction   │
     │    of idle limiter windows, a store that scales beyond SQLite's single  │
     │    writer.                                                              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Also note how to run and test: dotnet run, dotnet test.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Deliberately out of scope                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Auth, observability, migrations tooling, Docker.                      │
     │ - MediatR, CQRS, repository generics, AutoMapper, FluentValidation:     │
     │   they add ceremony with no payoff at this size.                        │
     │ - GET-by-id endpoint (not in the spec).                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Verification                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ 1. dotnet build and dotnet test are green (limiter, dedup, concurrency, │
     │    validation, API tests).                                              │
     │ 2. dotnet run, then via Swagger or the .http file:                      │
     │    - POST a reservation: 201 Created.                                   │
     │    - POST it again: 200 Duplicate.                                      │
     │    - Change the price and POST: 200 Updated.                            │
     │    - POST with an older updatedAtUtc: 200 Stale.                        │
     │    - Loop 101 POSTs for one supplier: the 101st returns 429 with        │
     │      Retry-After.                                                       │
     │    - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId} returns the expected      │
     │      counts.                                                            │
     │ 3. Inspect reservations.db (e.g. sqlite3) to confirm there is one row   │
     │    per key and the stats counters match.                                │
     │ 4. Add *.db to .gitignore.                                              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Working with Claude Code (assignment requirement)                       │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Use Sonnet 5.5 for the session, since the supplied key blocks other   │
     │   models.                                                               │
     │ - Prompt in small steps (one plan step each) and review each diff       │
     │   before moving on.                                                     │
     │ - Ask it to justify choices such as sliding log vs fixed window, and    │
     │   the transaction/locking approach.                                     │
     │ - Push back where you disagree, and record it for README section 2.     │
     │ - Don't edit the transcript. Run /export at the end and submit it with  │
     │   the repo and the README.                                              │
     │ - Initialize git early, with small commits per step.                    │

● Real SQLite is the better choice for the repository and API tests, since the
  dedup logic, locking and decimal round-trip live in the SQL and the
  transaction, and a mock would only verify my own scripted expectations. I'd
  keep fakes only for the rate limiter and the orthogonal branching in
  IngestionService. Should I keep SQLite for the repository and API tests, or
  switch? · summary

● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · How should the dedup and stats tests run? → Real SQLite for repo/API 
     tests, fakes for limiter + service (Recommended)
● The plan already reflects that choice, so I'm submitting it for approval.

     │ (IExceptionHandler -> ProblemDetails)                                   │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api.Tests/    NUnit                                 │
     │ README.md                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step-by-step                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 1. Scaffold and packages                                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Delete the weather sample from Program.cs. Keep Swagger in            │
     │   Development.                                                          │
     │ - Add packages: Dapper, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.                          │
     │ - Create the NUnit test project (dotnet new nunit) with NUnit,          │
     │   NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk,                            │
     │   Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing,                                     │
     │   Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing. Reference the API project  │
     │   and add it to the .sln.                                               │
     │ - Add public partial class Program; so WebApplicationFactory can see    │
     │   it.                                                                   │
     │ - Why: a clean baseline before any logic. TimeProvider.Testing lets us  │
     │   test the 60s window without sleeping.                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 2. Domain and contracts                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Reservation as an immutable record (SupplierId, ReservationId,        │
     │   RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut, Price (decimal), UpdatedAtUtc, plus a      │
     │   SameDetailsAs(other) method).                                         │
     │ - IngestStatus { Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale, Throttled }.       │
     │ - Request DTO with DataAnnotations plus IValidatableObject for checkOut │
     │   > checkIn. [ApiController] then gives automatic 400 ProblemDetails.   │
     │ - Use DateTimeOffset and normalize to UTC at the boundary. Use decimal  │
     │   for money.                                                            │
     │ - Why: keeps the HTTP contract separate from the domain and avoids a    │
     │   validation library for 4 rules.                                       │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 3. Data layer (Dapper and SQLite)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISqliteConnectionFactory reads the connection string from config      │
     │   (Data Source=reservations.db). Tests override it with a temp file.    │
     │ - DatabaseInitializer runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS at startup:       │
     │   - Reservations(SupplierId, ReservationId, RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut,  │
     │     Price, UpdatedAtUtc, PRIMARY KEY (SupplierId, ReservationId))       │
     │   - SupplierStats(SupplierId PRIMARY KEY, Ingested INTEGER, Throttled   │
     │     INTEGER)                                                            │
     │ - Dapper type handlers: DateTimeOffset stored as ISO-8601 UTC text      │
     │   (sortable and comparable). decimal stored as TEXT to avoid REAL float │
     │   drift. Verify round-trips with a test.                                │
     │ - IReservationRepository.UpsertAsync(reservation) runs in one write     │
     │   transaction:                                                          │
     │   a. SELECT the existing row by key.                                    │
     │   b. None: INSERT, giving Created.                                      │
     │   c. Identical: nothing is written, giving Duplicate.                   │
     │   d. Incoming updatedAtUtc is older: nothing is written, giving Stale.  │
     │   e. Otherwise UPDATE, giving Updated.                                  │
     │   f. For Created and Updated, increment SupplierStats.Ingested in the   │
     │      same transaction (atomic upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE  │
     │      SET Ingested = Ingested + 1).                                      │
     │ - ISupplierStatsRepository: IncrementThrottledAsync, GetAsync (zeros if │
     │   no row).                                                              │
     │ - Concurrency: the SELECT-then-write must not race (two identical       │
     │   concurrent requests must yield exactly one Created). Use an immediate │
     │   (write-locking) transaction. Confirm that Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's     │
     │   chosen isolation level really takes the write lock up front, and      │
     │   prove it with the concurrency test in Step 7. If it doesn't, fall     │
     │   back to a per-key SemaphoreSlim.                                      │
     │ - Also enable PRAGMA busy_timeout so concurrent writers wait instead of │
     │   throwing "database is locked".                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 4. Rate limiter (the interesting part)                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISupplierRateLimiter.TryAcquire(supplierId) ->                        │
     │   RateLimitResult(Allowed, RetryAfter).                                 │
     │ - SlidingWindowRateLimiter implements the sliding window log algorithm  │
     │   (singleton): one log of accepted-request timestamps per supplier.     │
     │   ConcurrentDictionary<string, Window>, where each window holds a       │
     │   Queue<DateTimeOffset> (the log, in chronological order) guarded by a  │
     │   lock.                                                                 │
     │   - On each call: dequeue timestamps <= now - 60s. If count >= limit,   │
     │     reject with RetryAfter = oldest + 60s - now. Otherwise enqueue now  │
     │     and allow.                                                          │
     │   - Rejected calls enqueue nothing (per your decision).                 │
     │ - RateLimitOptions (limit = 100, window = 60s) bound via IOptions, so   │
     │   tests can use small values if needed.                                 │
     │ - Inject TimeProvider (built into .NET 8) instead of calling            │
     │   DateTime.UtcNow.                                                      │
     │ - Why a sliding log over a fixed window: the spec says "any rolling     │
     │   60-second window". A fixed window allows 200 requests across a        │
     │   boundary. Memory is bounded at 100 timestamps per supplier.           │
     │ - Known limitation (README): in-memory state is lost on restart and not │
     │   shared across instances. Idle windows are never evicted, which is     │
     │   fine at this scale.                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 5. Ingestion service                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ IReservationIngestionService.IngestAsync(Reservation) orchestrates:     │
     │ 1. limiter.TryAcquire(supplierId). If denied,                           │
     │    stats.IncrementThrottledAsync, then return Throttled(retryAfter).    │
     │ 2. Otherwise reservationRepo.UpsertAsync and return the outcome.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ It returns a small result type (status plus optional RetryAfter), not   │
     │ exceptions. Exceptions are for exceptional cases only. Why this layer:  │
     │ the controller stays trivial and the logic is unit-testable with fakes. │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 6. Controller and error handling                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest maps the outcome:                       │
     │   - Created: 201 with a body and no Location header (use                │
     │     StatusCode(201, body), not CreatedAtAction).                        │
     │   - Updated, Duplicate, Stale: 200.                                     │
     │   - Throttled: 429 with a Retry-After header and ProblemDetails.        │
     │   - Body: { status, supplierId, reservationId }.                        │
     │ - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId} returns { supplierId,        │
     │   ingested, throttled }.                                                │
     │ - GlobalExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, .NET 8) turns unexpected   │
     │   errors into a 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace leaked. Log the  │
     │   exception.                                                            │
     │ - Register everything in Program.cs through small AddXxx extension      │
     │   methods. Add CancellationToken through the stack.                     │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 7. Tests (the grader's confidence signal)                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ All tests are NUnit: [TestFixture], [SetUp]/[TearDown] for a fresh temp │
     │ DB per test, [TestCase] for validation variants, Assert.That(...,       │
     │ Is...) constraints. Concurrency tests use Task.WhenAll. Don't mark      │
     │ fixtures that share a DB or WebApplicationFactory as [Parallelizable].  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Unit, rate limiter (FakeTimeProvider):                                  │
     │ - 100 calls allowed, 101st rejected with a sensible RetryAfter.         │
     │ - After advancing 60s the supplier is allowed again, and the window is  │
     │   truly rolling (requests at t=0 and t=30 expire independently).        │
     │ - Suppliers are isolated from each other.                               │
     │ - Rejected calls don't extend the window.                               │
     │ - Concurrency: 300 parallel calls produce exactly 100 allowed.          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Integration (WebApplicationFactory with a temp-file SQLite DB per test  │
     │ class):                                                                 │
     │ - Created (201), then identical resend (200 Duplicate, with proof no    │
     │   write happened, e.g. ingested stat unchanged and the row unchanged),  │
     │   then changed price (200 Updated, row updated), then older             │
     │   updatedAtUtc (Stale, row unchanged).                                  │
     │ - Same reservationId from two different suppliers gives two independent │
     │   rows (one can't overwrite the other).                                 │
     │ - Concurrency: N parallel identical ingests produce exactly 1 Created,  │
     │   N-1 Duplicate, and ingested == 1.                                     │
     │ - 101st request from a supplier gets 429 with Retry-After. Another      │
     │   supplier is unaffected. Stats show ingested=100, throttled=1.         │
     │ - Validation: missing fields, checkOut == checkIn, checkOut < checkIn   │
     │   and negative price each return 400. checkOut one tick after checkIn   │
     │   is accepted.                                                          │
     │ - 201 response has no Location header.                                  │
     │ - Stats for an unknown supplier return zeros.                           │
     │ - Decimal and date round-trip fidelity through SQLite.                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 8. README (half a page, as the assignment requires)                │

● Step 2 is done and dotnet build passes with 0 warnings and 0 errors. I stopped
  there. I haven't run any of this code yet, because nothing calls it until the
  controller exists.

  Domain (Domain/)
  - Reservation.cs is an immutable record with the composite identity
    (SupplierId, ReservationId). SameDetailsAs(other) compares everything except
    the identity: room, check-in, check-out, price and UpdatedAtUtc. The check
    is on the instant, so 10:00+02:00 equals 08:00Z. Step 3's repository will
    use it to decide between Duplicate and Update.
  - IngestStatus.cs has Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale and Throttled.

  Contracts (Contracts/)
  - IngestReservationRequest.cs:
    - Strings must be non-empty, and whitespace-only is rejected.
    - Dates and price are nullable with [Required], so a missing field gives a
      400 instead of silently becoming 0001-01-01 or 0.
    - price >= 0 is enforced.
    - IValidatableObject enforces that checkOut is strictly after checkIn, so
      equal values are rejected.
    - ToReservation() trims the ids and normalizes all timestamps to UTC.
  - IngestReservationResponse.cs returns { status, supplierId, reservationId }.
    The status is serialized as a string such as "Duplicate", not a number.
  - SupplierStatsResponse.cs returns { supplierId, ingested, throttled }.

  Things to know
  - Cross-field check is unconfirmed. I haven't confirmed that ASP.NET Core
    still runs the cross-field checkOut check when a property-level error is
    also present. In that case you might see only the field errors and not the
    date-order error. I wrote the check defensively, so it doesn't crash on
    missing values. Step 7's validation tests will confirm the actual behavior.
  - Validation tests wait until Step 7. The plan puts them there, and none exist
    yet.
  - Range on price uses double. Checking price >= 0 through a double is exact
    for 0, and prices that large can't be stored anyway. If you'd rather keep
    all rules in Validate(), say so and I'll move it.

     │ Reservations Ingest API: Implementation Plan                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Context                                                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Mize home assignment: an ASP.NET Core (.NET 8) Web API on SQLite with   │
     │ Dapper (required by the assignment) that sits in front of a             │
     │ reservations table and handles two problems: duplicate supplier updates │
     │ and over-eager suppliers.                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest: save, dedup, update, and throttle at   │
     │   more than 100 requests per rolling 60s per supplier.                  │
     │ - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId}: ingested vs throttled       │
     │   counts.                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The repo is a blank webapi template (ReservationsHandler.Api, net8.0,   │
     │ Swagger, weather sample in Program.cs). There are no Dapper, SQLite or  │
     │ test projects yet.                                                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Scope: 2-3 days, so a clean structure, sound concurrency, and focused   │
     │ tests. No auth, observability or migrations tooling.                    │

     │                                                                         │
     │ Why the composite key                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The spec's "same reservationId" could be read as reservationId alone.   │
     │ But ids are issued by each supplier independently, so collisions across │
     │ suppliers are realistic. Keying on reservationId alone would let        │
     │ supplier B silently overwrite supplier A's record and muddy             │
     │ per-supplier stats. A reservation is therefore identified by who sent   │
     │ it plus their id. The alternative (global key plus a 409 when the       │
     │ supplier differs) was rejected as extra rules the spec never asked for. │
     │ This goes in the README.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ My assumptions (to list in the README)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Identity is (supplierId, reservationId). Different suppliers may      │
     │   reuse the same reservation id, and cannot update each other's         │
     │   records.                                                              │
     │ - "Same details" means roomId, checkIn, checkOut, price and             │
     │   updatedAtUtc are all equal. Equal updatedAtUtc with other fields      │
     │   different is treated as an Update (the spec says different details    │
     │   means update).                                                        │
     │ - Order of checks is validate, then throttle, then ingest.              │
     │   - Throttle must precede all DB access, since its purpose is to        │
     │     protect the DB.                                                     │
     │   - Validate must precede throttle because the limiter keys on          │
     │     supplierId, which an invalid body may not have.                     │
     │   - Tradeoff: a supplier flooding invalid requests is not throttled.    │
     │     Those requests are cheap (no DB, no state), so this is accepted and │
     │     documented.                                                         │
     │ - Supplier ids are matched exactly (case-sensitive, trimmed).           │
     │ - Validation rules: required non-empty strings, checkOut strictly after │
     │   checkIn (equal values are rejected), price >= 0.                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Target structure                                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Single API project with folders (a four-project Clean Architecture      │
     │ would be over-engineering here), plus one test project.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ ReservationsHandler.sln                                                 │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api/                                                │
     │   Program.cs                      composition root only (extension      │
     │ methods for DI)                                                         │
     │   Controllers/ReservationsController.cs   thin: maps outcome -> HTTP    │
     │   Contracts/                      IngestReservationRequest,             │
     │ IngestReservationResponse, SupplierStatsResponse                        │
     │   Domain/                         Reservation (record), IngestStatus    │
     │ enum                                                                    │
     │   Services/                       IReservationIngestionService + impl   │
     │ (orchestration)                                                         │
     │   RateLimiting/                   ISupplierRateLimiter,                 │
     │ SlidingWindowRateLimiter, RateLimitOptions                              │
     │   Data/                           ISqliteConnectionFactory,             │
     │ DatabaseInitializer, DapperTypeHandlers,                                │
     │                                   IReservationRepository + impl,        │
     │ ISupplierStatsRepository + impl                                         │
     │   Infrastructure/                 GlobalExceptionHandler                │
     │ (IExceptionHandler -> ProblemDetails)                                   │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api.Tests/    NUnit                                 │
     │ README.md                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Testing rule (applies to every step)                                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Every step ends with a "Unit tests" sub-step covering the code that     │
     │ step generated, written before moving on. If a step produced nothing    │
     │ unit-testable (Step 1), it says so and writes none. A step is only done │
     │ when dotnet build and dotnet test are green.                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Unit tests are fast, need no DB or HTTP, and use hand-written fakes   │
     │   (no mocking library) and FakeTimeProvider. They live in the test      │
     │   project in folders that mirror the source folders (Domain/,           │
     │   Contracts/, RateLimiting/, Services/, Controllers/, Data/).           │
     │ - Integration tests (real SQLite temp file, WebApplicationFactory) are  │
     │   all kept in Step 7. Anything that needs the database or full HTTP     │
     │   pipeline waits until then, even when it belongs to an earlier step's  │
     │   code (repository SQL, initializer, round trips, end-to-end status     │
     │   codes).                                                               │
     │ - NUnit conventions: [TestFixture], [SetUp]/[TearDown], [TestCase] for  │
     │   variants, Assert.That(..., Is...). Don't mark fixtures that share     │
     │   state as [Parallelizable].                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step-by-step                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 1. Scaffold and packages                                           │
     │                                                                         │

     │   Development.                                                          │
     │ - Add packages: Dapper, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.                          │
     │ - Create the NUnit test project (dotnet new nunit) with NUnit,          │
     │   NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk,                            │
     │   Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing,                                     │
     │   Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing. Reference the API project  │
     │   and add it to the .sln.                                               │
     │ - Add public partial class Program; so WebApplicationFactory can see    │
     │   it.                                                                   │
     │ - Why: a clean baseline before any logic. TimeProvider.Testing lets us  │
     │   test the 60s window without sleeping.                                 │
     │ - Unit tests: none, since there is no logic yet. (Done.)                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 2. Domain and contracts                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Reservation as an immutable record (SupplierId, ReservationId,        │
     │   RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut, Price (decimal), UpdatedAtUtc, plus a      │
     │   SameDetailsAs(other) method).                                         │
     │ - IngestStatus { Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale, Throttled }.       │
     │ - Request DTO with DataAnnotations plus IValidatableObject for checkOut │
     │   > checkIn. [ApiController] then gives automatic 400 ProblemDetails.   │
     │ - Use DateTimeOffset and normalize to UTC at the boundary. Use decimal  │
     │   for money.                                                            │
     │ - Why: keeps the HTTP contract separate from the domain and avoids a    │
     │   validation library for 4 rules.                                       │
     │ - Code is already written. Unit tests still to write (backfill, do      │
     │   next):                                                                │
     │   - Reservation.SameDetailsAs: identical gives true. Each single field  │
     │     differing (room, checkIn, checkOut, price, updatedAtUtc) gives      │
     │     false, as a [TestCase] per field. Same instant in different offsets │
     │     is equal. 450.00m equals 450.0m. Identity fields                    │
     │     (supplier/reservation id) are ignored.                              │
     │   - IngestReservationRequest validation, via                            │
     │     Validator.TryValidateObject(..., validateAllProperties: true):      │
     │     valid request passes. Each missing field fails. Empty and           │
     │     whitespace strings fail. checkOut == checkIn and checkOut < checkIn │
     │     fail. checkOut one tick after checkIn passes. Negative price        │
     │     fails, price 0 passes.                                              │
     │   - ToReservation(): ids trimmed, non-UTC offsets normalized to UTC.    │
     │   - Whether MVC still reports the cross-field error alongside property  │
     │     errors is an HTTP-pipeline behavior, so it is verified in Step 7.   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 3. Data layer (Dapper and SQLite)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISqliteConnectionFactory reads the connection string from config      │
     │   (Data Source=reservations.db). Tests override it with a temp file.    │
     │ - DatabaseInitializer runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS at startup:       │
     │   - Reservations(SupplierId, ReservationId, RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut,  │
     │     Price, UpdatedAtUtc, PRIMARY KEY (SupplierId, ReservationId))       │
     │   - SupplierStats(SupplierId PRIMARY KEY, Ingested INTEGER, Throttled   │
     │     INTEGER)                                                            │
     │ - Dapper type handlers: DateTimeOffset stored as ISO-8601 UTC text      │
     │   (sortable and comparable). decimal stored as TEXT to avoid REAL float │
     │   drift. Verify round-trips with a test.                                │
     │ - IReservationRepository.UpsertAsync(reservation) runs in one write     │
     │   transaction:                                                          │
     │   a. SELECT the existing row by key.                                    │
     │   b. None: INSERT, giving Created.                                      │
     │   c. Identical: nothing is written, giving Duplicate.                   │
     │   d. Incoming updatedAtUtc is older: nothing is written, giving Stale.  │
     │   e. Otherwise UPDATE, giving Updated.                                  │
     │   f. For Created and Updated, increment SupplierStats.Ingested in the   │
     │      same transaction (atomic upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE  │
     │      SET Ingested = Ingested + 1).                                      │
     │ - ISupplierStatsRepository: IncrementThrottledAsync, GetAsync (zeros if │
     │   no row).                                                              │
     │ - Concurrency: the SELECT-then-write must not race (two identical       │
     │   concurrent requests must yield exactly one Created). Use an immediate │
     │   (write-locking) transaction. Confirm that Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's     │
     │   chosen isolation level really takes the write lock up front, and      │
     │   prove it with the concurrency test in Step 7. If it doesn't, fall     │
     │   back to a per-key SemaphoreSlim.                                      │
     │ - Also enable PRAGMA busy_timeout so concurrent writers wait instead of │
     │   throwing "database is locked".                                        │
     │ - Unit tests: only the parts that need no database. The DateTimeOffset  │
     │   and decimal type handlers' SetValue and Parse (UTC normalization,     │
     │   ISO-8601 text output, no precision loss on values like 450.10m,       │
     │   malformed text throws). The connection factory returns a connection   │
     │   with the configured connection string. The repositories, initializer  │
     │   and real round trips need SQLite, so they are integration tests in    │
     │   Step 7.                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 4. Rate limiter (the interesting part)                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - ISupplierRateLimiter.TryAcquire(supplierId) ->                        │
     │   RateLimitResult(Allowed, RetryAfter).                                 │
     │ - SlidingWindowRateLimiter implements the sliding window log algorithm  │
     │   (singleton): one log of accepted-request timestamps per supplier.     │
     │   ConcurrentDictionary<string, Window>, where each window holds a       │
     │   Queue<DateTimeOffset> (the log, in chronological order) guarded by a  │
     │   lock.                                                                 │
     │   - On each call: dequeue timestamps <= now - 60s. If count >= limit,   │
     │     reject with RetryAfter = oldest + 60s - now. Otherwise enqueue now  │
     │     and allow.                                                          │
     │   - Rejected calls enqueue nothing (per your decision).                 │
     │ - RateLimitOptions (limit = 100, window = 60s) bound via IOptions, so   │
     │   tests can use small values if needed.                                 │
     │ - Inject TimeProvider (built into .NET 8) instead of calling            │
     │   DateTime.UtcNow.                                                      │
     │ - Why a sliding log over a fixed window: the spec says "any rolling     │
     │   60-second window". A fixed window allows 200 requests across a        │
     │   boundary. Memory is bounded at 100 timestamps per supplier.           │
     │ - Known limitation (README): in-memory state is lost on restart and not │
     │   shared across instances. Idle windows are never evicted, which is     │
     │   fine at this scale.                                                   │
     │ - Unit tests (FakeTimeProvider, no DB):                                 │
     │   - 100 calls allowed, 101st rejected with a sensible RetryAfter.       │
     │   - After advancing 60s the supplier is allowed again, and the window   │
     │     is truly rolling (requests at t=0 and t=30 expire independently).   │
     │   - Boundary: a timestamp exactly 60s old has expired.                  │
     │   - Suppliers are isolated from each other.                             │
     │   - Rejected calls don't extend the window.                             │
     │   - Small custom RateLimitOptions are honored.                          │
     │   - Concurrency: 300 parallel calls produce exactly 100 allowed.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 5. Ingestion service                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ IReservationIngestionService.IngestAsync(Reservation) orchestrates:     │
     │ 1. limiter.TryAcquire(supplierId). If denied,                           │
     │    stats.IncrementThrottledAsync, then return Throttled(retryAfter).    │
     │ 2. Otherwise reservationRepo.UpsertAsync and return the outcome.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ It returns a small result type (status plus optional RetryAfter), not   │
     │ exceptions. Exceptions are for exceptional cases only. Why this layer:  │
     │ the controller stays trivial and the logic is unit-testable with fakes. │
     │ - Unit tests (hand-written fake limiter and fake repositories):         │
     │   - Limiter allows, so the repository is called and its outcome is      │
     │     returned unchanged (Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale).            │
     │   - Limiter denies, so the result is Throttled with the RetryAfter, the │
     │     throttled counter is incremented exactly once, and the repository   │
     │     is never called.                                                    │
     │   - The limiter is asked with the reservation's supplierId.             │
     │   - The cancellation token is passed through.                           │
     │   - A repository exception propagates (not swallowed).                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 6. Controller and error handling                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest maps the outcome:                       │
     │   - Created: 201 with a body and no Location header (use                │
     │     StatusCode(201, body), not CreatedAtAction).                        │
     │   - Updated, Duplicate, Stale: 200.                                     │
     │   - Throttled: 429 with a Retry-After header and ProblemDetails.        │
     │   - Body: { status, supplierId, reservationId }.                        │
     │ - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId} returns { supplierId,        │
     │   ingested, throttled }.                                                │
     │ - GlobalExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, .NET 8) turns unexpected   │
     │   errors into a 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace leaked. Log the  │
     │   exception.                                                            │
     │ - Register everything in Program.cs through small AddXxx extension      │
     │   methods. Add CancellationToken through the stack.                     │
     │ - Unit tests (controller called directly with a fake service, no HTTP): │
     │   - Each status maps to the right result: Created gives 201 with the    │
     │     body and no Location header. Updated, Duplicate and Stale give 200  │
     │     with the matching status. Throttled gives 429 with a Retry-After    │
     │     header (whole seconds, rounded up) and ProblemDetails.              │
     │   - The request is mapped to the domain Reservation (normalized) before │
     │     the service is called.                                              │
     │   - Stats endpoint returns the counts from a fake stats repository, and │
     │     zeros pass through.                                                 │
     │   - GlobalExceptionHandler: an unexpected exception yields a 500        │
     │     ProblemDetails with no stack trace or message leaked, and the       │
     │     exception is logged.                                                │
     │   - Full end-to-end HTTP behavior is covered in Step 7.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 7. Integration tests (the grader's confidence signal)              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Only integration tests are written here. All unit tests were written in │
     │ their own steps. Each test class gets a fresh temp-file SQLite DB via   │
     │ WebApplicationFactory ([SetUp]/[TearDown]). Concurrency tests use       │
     │ Task.WhenAll. Don't mark these fixtures [Parallelizable].               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Integration (WebApplicationFactory with a temp-file SQLite DB per test  │
     │ class):                                                                 │
     │ - Repository and initializer against real SQLite: schema is created     │
     │   idempotently, one row per (supplierId, reservationId), and            │
     │   SupplierStats counters are atomic.                                    │
     │ - Created (201), then identical resend (200 Duplicate, with proof no    │
     │   write happened, e.g. ingested stat unchanged and the row unchanged),  │
     │   then changed price (200 Updated, row updated), then older             │
     │   updatedAtUtc (Stale, row unchanged).                                  │
     │ - Same reservationId from two different suppliers gives two independent │
     │   rows (one can't overwrite the other).                                 │
     │ - Concurrency: N parallel identical ingests produce exactly 1 Created,  │
     │   N-1 Duplicate, and ingested == 1.                                     │
     │ - 101st request from a supplier gets 429 with Retry-After. Another      │
     │   supplier is unaffected. Stats show ingested=100, throttled=1.         │
     │ - Validation over real HTTP: missing fields, checkOut == checkIn,       │
     │   checkOut < checkIn and negative price each return 400 ProblemDetails. │
     │   checkOut one tick after checkIn is accepted. Also confirm the         │
     │   checkOut error is reported when other fields are invalid too (see     │
     │   Step 2 note).                                                         │
     │ - An unexpected failure returns 500 ProblemDetails over HTTP.           │
     │ - 201 response has no Location header.                                  │
     │ - Stats for an unknown supplier return zeros.                           │
     │ - Decimal and date round-trip fidelity through SQLite.                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 8. README (half a page, as the assignment requires)                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Three sections:                                                         │
     │ 1. Assumptions: the list above, with reasons.                           │
     │ 2. Claude suggestions I disagreed with or changed: fill this in         │
     │    honestly during the session.                                         │
     │ 3. With more time: distributed limiter (Redis), migrations              │
     │    (DbUp/FluentMigrator), idempotency/outbox, auth, metrics, eviction   │
     │    of idle limiter windows, a store that scales beyond SQLite's single  │
     │    writer.                                                              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Also note how to run and test: dotnet run, dotnet test.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Deliberately out of scope                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Auth, observability, migrations tooling, Docker.                      │
     │ - MediatR, CQRS, repository generics, AutoMapper, FluentValidation:     │
     │   they add ceremony with no payoff at this size.                        │
     │ - GET-by-id endpoint (not in the spec).                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Verification                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ 1. dotnet build and dotnet test are green after every step (unit tests  │
     │    per step, integration tests from Step 7).                            │
     │ 2. dotnet run, then via Swagger or the .http file:                      │
     │    - POST a reservation: 201 Created.                                   │
     │    - POST it again: 200 Duplicate.                                      │
     │    - Change the price and POST: 200 Updated.                            │
     │    - POST with an older updatedAtUtc: 200 Stale.                        │
     │    - Loop 101 POSTs for one supplier: the 101st returns 429 with        │
     │      Retry-After.                                                       │
     │    - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId} returns the expected      │
     │      counts.                                                            │

✻ Sautéed for 1m 4s · done Wednesday 6:28 PM

> explain test CheckOutComparison_UsesInstants_NotOffsets                       

● CheckOutComparison_UsesInstants_NotOffsets checks that the
  check-out-after-check-in rule compares real moments in time. It does not
  compare the clock text.

  The setup
  - Check-in is the default 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z, which is midnight UTC.
  - Check-out is 2026-08-01T02:00:00+02:00, which is 2 AM at a UTC+2 offset.
  - To a human the check-out looks later, because 02:00 is after 00:00. But
    02:00 at +02:00 is the same instant as 00:00 UTC. The two timestamps are the
    same moment.
  - The rule says check-out must be strictly after check-in, and equal values
    are rejected. So this request must fail, with the error on CheckOut. That is
    what the test asserts.

  Why it matters
  - Suppliers can send any offset. If the code compared the wall-clock part
    (DateTime, or the text), it would see 02:00 > 00:00 and accept a zero-night
    stay.
  - DateTimeOffset comparison with <= already works on the UTC instant, so the
    code is correct today. The test guards against a later refactor to something
    like CheckOut.Value.DateTime <= CheckIn.Value.DateTime, which would break
    this silently.

  A related check
  SameDetailsAs_ComparesInstants_NotOffsets in ReservationTests covers the same
  idea for duplicate detection. It makes sure 02:00+02:00 and 00:00Z count as
  identical details, so a supplier that resends the same reservation with a
  different offset still gets Duplicate and not a needless update.

  A limit of the test
  It only has an offset on the check-out. A case where the offset flips the
  order (for example check-in at 01:00+00:00 and check-out at 02:00+03:00, which
  is 23:00 UTC the day before) would be a stronger version, since the
  wall-clock comparison would accept it and the instant comparison would reject
  it. I can add that if you want.

● Step 3 is done, and I stopped before Step 4. dotnet test shows all 71 tests
  passing (35 from before, 36 new).

  What was built (Data/ and Domain/)
  - Domain:
    - ReservationChangeEvaluator holds the pure dedup rules and returns Created,
      Duplicate, Stale or Updated.
    - SupplierStats is the counters record.
  - Data:
    - SqliteConnectionFactory takes its connection string from appsettings.json
      (Data Source=reservations.db).
    - DatabaseInitializer creates the two tables idempotently at startup.
      Reservations has primary key (SupplierId, ReservationId).
    - ReservationRepository.UpsertAsync runs the select and the write in one
      transaction and increments Ingested in that same transaction. Duplicate
      and stale requests write nothing.
    - SupplierStatsRepository does an atomic throttled increment, and its
      GetAsync returns zeros for an unknown supplier.
  - Wiring: AddDataAccess() and InitializeDatabaseAsync() are called from
    Program.cs.

  Two risks from the plan, both checked on a real SQLite file
  - Dapper type handlers: this part of the plan didn't work.
    - Dapper ignores a custom handler's SetValue for built-in types. Dates were
      stored as 2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00, and my own Parse then rejected them.
    - I replaced the handlers with a pure SqliteValueConverter that formats and
      parses explicitly.
    - This also avoids process-wide Dapper state.
    - It's worth a line in the README under "things Claude Code suggested that I
      changed".
  - Write lock:
    - BeginTransaction(deferred: false) is a BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and it works. 20
      parallel identical upserts gave exactly 1 Created and 19 Duplicate, with
      ingested == 1.
    - I also confirmed the test can fail. With deferred: true it fails with
      SQLite Error 5: 'database is locked'.
    - I'd already restored deferred: false when I wrote this up.

  Things to know
  - I deleted the scratch tests that did this checking. Their real versions
    (repository, initializer, concurrency) come in Step 7. The plan lists them.
  - I updated the plan file and CLAUDE.md to match the code. CLAUDE.md also
    reminds me to call SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() before deleting temp
    databases in tests.
  - The first test run had two failures, both in my own tests. I passed double
    values to a decimal test and the trailing zero in 450.00 was lost. I
    switched to real decimal literals and nothing in the converter changed.
  - Microsoft.Data.Sqlite already applies a 30-second busy timeout when it opens
    a connection, so I didn't add a PRAGMA busy_timeout. The comment in
    SqliteConnectionFactory.cs says so.
  - I haven't started the app or run it through Swagger. Nothing calls the
    repositories yet; the controller arrives in Step 6.

  Say "go" for Step 4, the rate limiter.

  one is a question I'll answer and then ask you about.

  Type handlers. I told you Dapper ignores custom handlers for built-in types,
  and that was incomplete. Dapper has a supported workaround,
  SqlMapper.RemoveTypeMap(type), which makes the handler apply. I should have

  verify them against a real file again.

✻ Crunched for 3m 57s · done Wednesday 8:18 PM

> why dose ReservationChangeEvaluator need a class and cant be a function under 
  ReservationRepository? also explain the DataServiceCollectionExtensions       
  class isnt it suppose to be on program.cs?                                    

● Both are judgment calls, and neither is forced. I'd keep both as they are, but
  I can see the case for changing them.

  ReservationChangeEvaluator: why not a method in ReservationRepository?

  It could be a private static method there, and it would work. C# has no free
  functions, so a "function" always lives inside some class. The real question
  is which class it belongs in. I put it in its own static class for three
  reasons:

  1. It's business logic, not persistence. The rules are "identical means
     Duplicate, older means Stale, otherwise Updated". They don't depend on SQL.
     The repository's job is to run the select, perform the write the rules
     call for, and commit.
  2. It's testable without a database. The 9 tests in
     ReservationChangeEvaluatorTests run in milliseconds. If the rules were
     private inside the repository, the only way to test them would be through
     SQLite, which means Step 7 integration tests with temp files. I could mark
     the method internal and expose it to the test project, but at that point
     it's a separate unit in everything but name.
  3. It stays readable. UpsertAsync currently reads as "open, lock, load,
     decide, write, commit", and the decide step is one line.

  The cost is one more type for a single method. If you'd rather have fewer
  types, there's a better home than the repository: a static method on
  Reservation itself, next to SameDetailsAs, for example
  Reservation.Evaluate(existing, incoming). It would keep the rules in the
  domain, stay DB-free and testable, and need no extra class. I can move it
  there if you like.

  DataServiceCollectionExtensions: isn't that supposed to be in Program.cs?

  It doesn't have to be. This is the standard .NET convention. AddControllers(),
  AddSwaggerGen() and AddDbContext() are all extension methods on
  IServiceCollection that hide their own registrations. Program.cs still calls
  it, in one line: builder.Services.AddDataAccess(). The class only holds the
  method body, not the decision to use it.

  The reasons for keeping it out of Program.cs:
  - Composition root stays readable. Program.cs should show the app's shape:
    controllers, Swagger, data access, rate limiter, exception handler. The
    details stay with the feature, such as the connection-string name, the
    singleton lifetimes, and the lazy resolution so test hosts can override the
    connection string.
  - It will grow. Steps 4 to 6 add the limiter, the ingestion service and the
    exception handler. Inline, Program.cs becomes a long list of registrations.
  - It's the plan's design. The plan says "Register everything in Program.cs
    through small AddXxx extension methods", so Steps 4 to 6 will add
    AddRateLimiting() and AddIngestion() in the same style.
  - InitializeDatabaseAsync lives there too. It's the startup hook that pairs
    with those registrations.

  At the current size, about 15 lines of registration, putting it inline in
  Program.cs would also be fine. The extension-method style pays off as the app
  grows.

  Do you want me to move either one? I've made no changes. Otherwise, say "go"
  for Step 4.
