     │   throttled request gets a 429 and never this body (the status          │
     │   description says so).                                                 │
     │ - Verified finding (offset-less timestamps): on a UTC+2 machine,        │
     │   "2026-07-01T10:15:00" (no offset) followed by the same instant        │
     │   written with Z returned Updated, not Duplicate: System.Text.Json      │
     │   reads an offset-less value as SERVER-LOCAL time. The spec's examples  │
     │   all carry Z, so this is an edge case.                                 │
     │   - DECISION (dropped for now): not validated, documented as a known    │
     │     limitation. A parse-time converter that rejected offset-less        │
     │     timestamps with a 400 (OffsetRequiredDateTimeOffsetConverter) was   │
     │     built, unit tested, mutation-checked and verified over real HTTP,   │
     │     then deliberately removed for scope: the spec's examples all carry  │
     │     Z and the field is named updatedAtUtc. It could not live in         │
     │     IngestReservationRequest.Validate() (nor in a custom validation     │
     │     attribute): the parsed DateTimeOffset of an offset-less value is    │
     │     identical to one written with the local offset, so the information  │
     │     is gone before any validation runs; a parse-time converter was the  │
     │     only reliable place. If revisited: reject with a 400 (strict,       │
     │     safest) or assume UTC (friendlier, but silently accepts ambiguity). │
     │   - README (Step 8), under assumptions/limitations: timestamps are      │
     │     expected to carry an explicit UTC offset (Z or +hh:mm), as in the   │
     │     assignment's examples. One without an offset is read as             │
     │     SERVER-LOCAL time by System.Text.Json, so a supplier that sends the │
     │     same instant in two styles (10:15:00 then 10:15:00Z) would get      │
     │     Updated instead of Duplicate on a server that does not run in UTC.  │
     │     With more time: reject offset-less timestamps with a 400 at parse   │
     │     time.                                                               │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest maps the outcome:                       │
     │   - Created: 201 with a body and no Location header (use                │
     │     StatusCode(201, body), not CreatedAtAction).                        │

     │   - Decision: no SupplierStatsService. The controller injects           │
     │     ISupplierStatsRepository directly. The endpoint is a read-only      │
     │     query with no business logic, so a service would be a pass-through  │
     │     (one class, one interface, one fake, tests that only test the       │
     │     delegation). The POST has a service because it has real             │
     │     orchestration (throttle, then write); symmetry alone is not a       │
     │     reason for a shallow layer. If logic ever appears (derived values,  │
     │     caching, authorization), extract a service then; the repository     │
     │     interface makes that a small refactor. Cost to record in the        │
     │     README: the controller depends on one service and one repository.   │
     │   - The controller owns the HTTP concerns: trim the route supplierId,   │
     │     and return 400 ProblemDetails for a blank one (the repository       │

     │     domain SupplierStats to SupplierStatsResponse (the two stay         │
     │     separate types by an earlier decision).                             │
     │ - GlobalExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, .NET 8) turns unexpected   │
     │   errors into a 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace leaked. Log the  │
     │   exception.                                                            │
     │   - Cancellation is not an error, and the framework already handles it  │
     │     (verified, so no special case in our handler): a scratch test with  │
     │     a real in-memory server cancelled the client request mid-flight.    │
     │     ASP.NET's exception middleware intercepted the                      │
     │     OperationCanceledException BEFORE IExceptionHandler was invoked (a  │
     │     probe handler recorded 0 calls), logged only at Debug ("The request │

     │     OCE branch would be dead code. A permanent version of that check    │
     │     (no error log, no 500, handler not invoked) belongs in the Step 7   │
     │     integration tests.                                                  │
     │   - Consuming IngestResult without !: use if (result.RetryAfter is { }  │
     │     retryAfter) for the 429 branch (this also removes the nullable from │
     │     the happy path), then Created gives 201 and everything else 200.    │
     │     Put the whole-seconds, rounded-up Retry-After conversion in one     │
     │     small helper with unit tests (1ms gives 1, 60s gives 60, 60.0001s   │
     │     gives 61).                                                          │
     │ - Register features in Program.cs. Use an AddXxx extension method only  │
     │   when a feature has non-trivial wiring (as with data access and rate   │
     │   limiting); a single registration goes inline. Add CancellationToken   │
     │   through the stack.                                                    │

     │     direct SQL assertions, pools cleared on dispose); it already        │
     │     registers the Dapper handlers, which matters for any direct         │
     │     repository use.                                                     │
     │   - Optional overrides via constructor arguments:                       │
     │     RateLimiting:PermitLimit through UseSetting (options are read once  │
     │     when the limiter is built, so it must be set before the host        │
     │     builds); a FakeTimeProvider through ConfigureTestServices(s =>      │
     │     s.AddSingleton<TimeProvider>(fake)) (the later registration wins    │
     │     over TryAddSingleton); a replacement IReservationRepository for the │
     │     failure test.                                                       │
     │   - Quiet logging: ConfigureLogging(l => l.ClearProviders()), so test   │
     │     output is not flooded by the Development Debug level.               │
     │ - A new factory per test ([SetUp]/[TearDown]). The limiter is a         │
     │   singleton whose state lives in memory, so sharing a factory would     │
     │   leak quota between tests. About 14 hosts start in a few seconds,      │
     │   which is acceptable.                                                  │
     │ - Direct database assertions through                                    │
     │   TempSqliteDatabase.ConnectionFactory plus Dapper (SELECT COUNT(*)     │
     │   FROM Reservations, the stored row, the SupplierStats row). This is    │
     │   how "nothing was written" is proven, not only inferred from a status  │
     │   code.                                                                 │
     │ - Helper to build the request body from the spec's shape (supplier,     │
     │   reservation id, price, updatedAtUtc, ...), with explicit UTC offsets. │
     │                                                                         │
     │ 7b. The integration tests (about 14; each asserts the HTTP result AND   │
     │ the database)                                                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Dedup                                                                   │
     │ 1. Create: POST a new reservation, expect 201, body Created, no         │
     │    Location header, one row stored with the right values (price 450.10, │
     │    dates in UTC).                                                       │
     │ 2. Duplicate, proven by what did NOT happen: resend identical details   │
     │    (also once with the price as 450 instead of 450.00, and once with    │
     │    the same instant in +02:00 notation), expect 200 Duplicate, still    │
     │    one row, unchanged, and SupplierStats.Ingested still 1.              │
     │ 3. Update: changed details with a newer updatedAtUtc, expect 200        │
     │    Updated, the row now holds the new values, Ingested 2.               │
     │ 4. Stale: an older updatedAtUtc with different details, expect 200      │
     │    Stale, the row unchanged, Ingested unchanged.                        │
     │ 5. Composite identity: the same reservationId from two suppliers gives  │
     │    two independent rows, and updating one leaves the other untouched.   │
     │ 6. Concurrency: 20 identical requests fired at once give exactly 1      │
     │    Created and 19 Duplicate, one row, Ingested 1. This is what proves   │
     │    the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction works.                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Throttle                                                                │
     │ 7. The assignment's rule, with the real limit of 100: 101 requests from │
     │ one supplier (distinct reservation ids). The first 100 are not          │
     │ throttled, the 101st returns 429 application/problem+json with a        │
     │ Retry-After header, the reservations table holds 100 rows (the          │
     │ throttled request wrote nothing), and the stats read ingested 100,      │
     │ throttled 1.                                                            │
     │ 8. Isolation: while that supplier is throttled, another supplier's      │
     │ request still succeeds.                                                 │
     │ 9. The window clears, and Retry-After is rounded up (uses               │
     │ FakeTimeProvider and PermitLimit 2, no sleeping): throttled at t=0      │
     │ gives Retry-After: 60; after advancing 30.5 s it is 30; after advancing │
     │ to 59.9999 s it is 1 (never 0); after 60 s the supplier is accepted     │
     │ again.                                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Errors and the rest                                                     │
     │ 10. Invalid input (3 cases): an empty object, checkOut == checkIn, and  │
     │ a negative price each return 400 application/problem+json, and nothing  │
     │ is stored.                                                              │
     │ 11. Stats for an unknown supplier return {ingested: 0, throttled: 0}; a │
     │ blank id returns 400.                                                   │
     │ 12. An unexpected failure returns a clean 500 (the one extra group you  │
     │ chose to keep): replace the repository with FakeReservationRepository   │
     │ that throws an exception carrying a secret-looking message; expect 500  │
     │ application/problem+json, and a body that contains neither the message  │
     │ nor the exception type nor a stack trace.                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ (The first request in every test also proves the application starts,    │
     │ the schema is created, and the Dapper handlers are registered, so no    │
     │ separate tests are needed for the initializer, the connection factory   │
     │ or the type handlers.)                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ 7c. Unit tests that STAY (about 32), and where                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Trim these four files to exactly these tests; delete everything else in │

     │ - Domain/ReservationTests.cs (12 cases, the dedup rules):               │

  2. Unit tests that stay (about 32): the dedup rules (12), the limiter
  algorithm including the 300-parallel test (6), the service orchestration (8),
  and the validation rules (6).

  3. Deleted: 12 test files (type handlers, connection factory, initializer,
  controller mapping, exception-handler unit tests, DI and options plumbing,
  logging, IngestResultTests) and 3 fakes that nothing uses afterward. The
  trade-off, which goes in the README, is that logging levels, option validation
  and Swagger lose their automated guards.

  4. Proof the tests work: I break the code on purpose in seven ways and confirm
  the specific test fails each time, then restore it. The breaks are: a
  duplicate that writes, no stale rule, a weaker transaction, a limiter off by
  one, a service that writes while throttled, the wrong limiter key, and a
  handler that leaks the exception message.

  5. Order of work:
  1. Build the factory and tests 1 and 2, and run them alone.
  2. Write tests 3 to 12.
  3. Trim the unit tests.
  4. Run the seven mutation checks.
  5. Update CLAUDE.md and do the final checks.

     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │     │ is throttled                 │                                  │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├─────┼──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │     │ Fake clock: the window       │ Retry-After 60, then 30, then 1  │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │ 9   │ clears                       │ (rounded up, never 0), accepted  │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │     │                              │ again after 60 s                 │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├─────┼──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │ 10  │ Invalid input (3 cases)      │ 400 problem+json, nothing stored │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├─────┼──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │ 11  │ Stats for an unknown         │ zeros, and 400                   │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │     │ supplier, and a blank id     │                                  │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ ├─────┼──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┤                                                                    │
     │ │ 12  │ Unexpected failure           │ clean 500, no message, type or   │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ │     │                              │ stack leaked                     │
     │   │                                                                     │
     │ └─────┴──────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────── │
     │ ───┘                                                                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Infrastructure: Integration/ReservationsApiFactory (a                   │
     │ WebApplicationFactory<Program>) with a temp-file database set through   │
     │ UseSetting,                                                             │
     │ optional PermitLimit, optional FakeTimeProvider, an optional            │

     │ One factory per test, because the limiter keeps its state in memory. It │
     │ reuses Support/TempSqliteDatabase.                                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ 2. Unit tests that stay (about 32)                                      │
     │                                                                         │

     │                                                                         │
     │ 4. Proof that the tests really protect the logic (mutation checks)      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Break the code on purpose, confirm the specific test fails, then        │

     │ ---                                                                     │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Appendix: the full build plan and its history (kept for the README; the │
     │ plan for this change is above)                                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Reservations Ingest API: Implementation Plan                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Context                                                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Mize home assignment: an ASP.NET Core (.NET 8) Web API on SQLite with   │
     │ Dapper (required by the assignment) that sits in front of a             │
     │ reservations table and handles two problems: duplicate supplier updates │
     │ and over-eager suppliers.                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest: save, dedup, update, and throttle at   │
     │   more than 100 requests per rolling 60s per supplier.                  │
     │ - GET /api/reservations/stats/{supplierId}: ingested vs throttled       │
     │   counts.                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The repo is a blank webapi template (ReservationsHandler.Api, net8.0,   │
     │ Swagger, weather sample in Program.cs). There are no Dapper, SQLite or  │
     │ test projects yet.                                                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Scope: 2-3 days, so a clean structure, sound concurrency, and focused   │
     │ tests. No auth, observability or migrations tooling.                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The assignment grades the Claude Code process as well as the code: the  │
     │ transcript, pushback and tradeoff judgment. Each step below is a        │
     │ natural prompt-sized unit. See "Working with Claude Code" at the end.   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Decisions (confirmed with you)                                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Topic: Stale updates                                                    │
     │ Decision: If updatedAtUtc is older than the stored one, do not write.   │
     │ Return a                                                                │
     │   Stale outcome.                                                        │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Throttle counting                                                │
     │ Decision: Only accepted requests fill the window, so it clears after    │
     │ 60s.                                                                    │
     │   Rejected ones don't extend it.                                        │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Limiter storage                                                  │
     │ Decision: In-memory, thread-safe, sliding-window log per supplier.      │
     │ README notes                                                            │
     │   that production needs external storage (e.g. Redis) for restarts and  │
     │ multiple                                                                │
     │    instances.                                                           │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Stats                                                            │
     │ Decision: ingested = created + updated. Duplicates and stale updates    │
     │ are not                                                                 │
     │   counted. Unknown supplier returns {ingested:0, throttled:0}.          │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Responses                                                        │
     │ Decision: 201 Created (no Location header), 200 Updated, 200 Duplicate, │
     │ 200                                                                     │
     │   Stale. Every success body has an explicit status. 429 + Retry-After   │
     │ for                                                                     │
     │   throttled. 400 ProblemDetails for invalid input.                      │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Test framework                                                   │
     │ Decision: NUnit                                                         │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Reservation identity                                             │
     │ Decision: Composite (supplierId, reservationId), see below.             │
     │ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │
     │ Topic: Test strategy (changed late, by you)                             │
     │ Decision: The assignment asks for "enough tests to give us confidence   │
     │ the dedup                                                               │
     │   and throttle logic actually work", for a 2-3 day exercise. So:        │
     │ integration                                                             │
     │   tests prove dedup and throttling end to end (real HTTP, real SQLite), │
     │ backed                                                                  │
     │   by a small pure-logic unit suite. The suite drops from 201 tests to   │
     │ about 46.                                                               │
     │    See Step 7.                                                          │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Why the composite key                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ The spec's "same reservationId" could be read as reservationId alone.   │
     │ But ids are issued by each supplier independently, so collisions across │
     │ suppliers are realistic. Keying on reservationId alone would let        │
     │ supplier B silently overwrite supplier A's record and muddy             │
     │ per-supplier stats. A reservation is therefore identified by who sent   │
     │ it plus their id. The alternative (global key plus a 409 when the       │
     │ supplier differs) was rejected as extra rules the spec never asked for. │
     │ This goes in the README.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ My assumptions (to list in the README)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Identity is (supplierId, reservationId). Different suppliers may      │
     │   reuse the same reservation id, and cannot update each other's         │
     │   records.                                                              │
     │ - "Same details" means roomId, checkIn, checkOut, price and             │
     │   updatedAtUtc are all equal. Equal updatedAtUtc with other fields      │
     │   different is treated as an Update (the spec says different details    │
     │   means update).                                                        │
     │ - Order of checks is validate, then throttle, then ingest.              │
     │   - Throttle must precede all DB access, since its purpose is to        │
     │     protect the DB.                                                     │
     │   - Validate must precede throttle because the limiter keys on          │
     │     supplierId, which an invalid body may not have.                     │
     │   - Tradeoff: a supplier flooding invalid requests is not throttled.    │
     │     Those requests are cheap (no DB, no state), so this is accepted and │
     │     documented.                                                         │
     │ - Supplier ids are matched exactly (case-sensitive, trimmed).           │
     │ - Validation rules: required non-empty strings, checkOut strictly after │
     │   checkIn (equal values are rejected), price >= 0.                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Target structure                                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Single API project with folders (a four-project Clean Architecture      │
     │ would be over-engineering here), plus one test project.                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ ReservationsHandler.sln                                                 │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api/                                                │
     │   Program.cs                      composition root only (extension      │
     │ methods for DI)                                                         │
     │   Controllers/ReservationsController.cs   thin: maps outcome -> HTTP    │
     │   Contracts/                      IngestReservationRequest,             │
     │ IngestReservationResponse, SupplierStatsResponse                        │
     │   Domain/                         Reservation (record), IngestStatus    │
     │ enum                                                                    │
     │   Services/                       IReservationIngestionService + impl   │
     │ (orchestration)                                                         │
     │   RateLimiting/                   IRateLimiter,                         │
     │ SlidingWindowRateLimiter, RateLimitOptions                              │
     │   Data/                           IDbConnectionFactory (+               │
     │ SqliteConnectionFactory), DatabaseInitializer, type handlers +          │
     │ DapperConfiguration,                                                    │
     │                                   IReservationRepository + impl,        │
     │ ISupplierStatsRepository + impl                                         │
     │   Infrastructure/                 GlobalExceptionHandler                │
     │ (IExceptionHandler -> ProblemDetails),                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ ApiControllersServiceCollectionExtensions (AddApiControllers: JSON-only │
     │ formatters, string enums),                                              │
     │                                   ApiDocumentationExtensions            │
     │ (AddApiDocumentation / UseApiDocumentation: Swagger setup)              │
     │ ReservationsHandler.Api.Tests/    NUnit                                 │
     │ README.md                                                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Testing rule (REVISED: this replaces the original "unit tests at the    │
     │ end of every step" rule)                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Steps 1-6 were built with a unit test for almost everything (201        │
     │ tests). That is more than a 2-3 day exercise needs, and it is the wrong │
     │ shape: most of those tests check plumbing, while the assignment wants   │
     │ confidence in dedup and throttling. The rule now is:                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Integration tests are the main evidence. They run the real            │
     │   application (WebApplicationFactory), real HTTP, and a real temp-file  │
     │   SQLite database, and they assert the behavior the assignment          │
     │   describes (see Step 7).                                               │
     │ - Unit tests only where a table of cases is clearer than an HTTP call   │
     │   and no infrastructure is needed: the dedup rules, the limiter         │
     │   algorithm (including its concurrency), the ingestion service's        │
     │   orchestration, and the request validation rules. About 32 tests in    │
     │   total.                                                                │
     │ - Do not unit test plumbing: DI wiring, options binding, type handlers, │
     │   the connection factory, logging, controller mapping, Swagger. If it   │
     │   is wrong, an integration test fails, and that is a better signal.     │
     │ - Hand-written fakes (no mocking library). NUnit conventions:           │
     │   [TestFixture], [SetUp]/[TearDown], [TestCase] for variants,           │
     │   Assert.That(..., Is...). Never mark fixtures that share a database, a │
     │   factory or a limiter as [Parallelizable].                             │
     │ - A change is done when dotnet build and dotnet test are green AND      │
     │   every test class also passes when run on its own (Dapper's registry   │
     │   is process-wide, so a full run can hide an order dependence).         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step-by-step                                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 1. Scaffold and packages                                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Delete the weather sample from Program.cs. Keep Swagger in            │
     │   Development.                                                          │
     │ - Add packages: Dapper, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.                          │
     │ - Create the NUnit test project (dotnet new nunit) with NUnit,          │
     │   NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk,                            │
     │   Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing,                                     │
     │   Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing. Reference the API project  │
     │   and add it to the .sln.                                               │
     │ - Add public partial class Program; so WebApplicationFactory can see    │
     │   it.                                                                   │
     │ - Why: a clean baseline before any logic. TimeProvider.Testing lets us  │
     │   test the 60s window without sleeping.                                 │
     │ - Unit tests: none, since there is no logic yet. (Done.)                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 2. Domain and contracts                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - Reservation as an immutable record (SupplierId, ReservationId,        │
     │   RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut, Price (decimal), UpdatedAtUtc, plus a      │
     │   SameDetailsAs(other) method).                                         │
     │ - IngestStatus { Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale, Throttled }.       │
     │ - Request DTO with DataAnnotations plus IValidatableObject for checkOut │
     │   > checkIn. [ApiController] then gives automatic 400 ProblemDetails.   │
     │ - Use DateTimeOffset and normalize to UTC at the boundary. Use decimal  │
     │   for money.                                                            │
     │ - Why: keeps the HTTP contract separate from the domain and avoids a    │
     │   validation library for 4 rules.                                       │
     │ - Code is already written. Unit tests still to write (backfill, do      │
     │   next):                                                                │
     │   - Reservation.SameDetailsAs: identical gives true. Each single field  │
     │     differing (room, checkIn, checkOut, price, updatedAtUtc) gives      │
     │     false, as a [TestCase] per field. Same instant in different offsets │
     │     is equal. 450.00m equals 450.0m. Identity fields                    │
     │     (supplier/reservation id) are ignored.                              │
     │   - IngestReservationRequest validation, via                            │
     │     Validator.TryValidateObject(..., validateAllProperties: true):      │
     │     valid request passes. Each missing field fails. Empty and           │
     │     whitespace strings fail. checkOut == checkIn and checkOut < checkIn │
     │     fail. checkOut one tick after checkIn passes. Negative price        │
     │     fails, price 0 passes.                                              │
     │   - ToReservation(): ids trimmed, non-UTC offsets normalized to UTC.    │
     │   - Whether MVC still reports the cross-field error alongside property  │
     │     errors is an HTTP-pipeline behavior, so it is verified in Step 7.   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 3. Data layer (Dapper and SQLite)                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - IDbConnectionFactory.OpenConnectionAsync() returns an open            │
     │   DbConnection. SqliteConnectionFactory is built by a lazy DI factory   │
     │   that reads ConnectionStrings:Reservations from the final              │
     │   IConfiguration (Data Source=reservations.db), so tests can override   │
     │   it with a temp file.                                                  │
     │ - DatabaseInitializer runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS at startup:       │
     │   - Reservations(SupplierId, ReservationId, RoomId, CheckIn, CheckOut,  │
     │     Price, UpdatedAtUtc, PRIMARY KEY (SupplierId, ReservationId))       │
     │   - SupplierStats(SupplierId PRIMARY KEY, Ingested INTEGER, Throttled   │
     │     INTEGER)                                                            │
     │ - Type handlers (kept, with a required workaround for dates):           │
     │   DateTimeOffsetTypeHandler (fixed-width ISO-8601 UTC text, sortable)   │
     │   is needed for reading and writing. A scratch test showed that Dapper  │
     │   does NOT call a handler's SetValue for built-in types unless the      │
     │   built-in mapping is removed first, so                                 │
     │   DapperConfiguration.RegisterTypeHandlers() calls                      │
     │   SqlMapper.RemoveTypeMap for DateTimeOffset (and its nullable) before  │
     │   AddTypeHandler. DecimalTypeHandler is read-only: experiments showed   │
     │   that without it Dapper cannot map the TEXT Price column into the      │
     │   record's decimal parameter (all cases failed), but that               │
     │   Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's native decimal write is already invariant     │
     │   text that round-trips exactly (checked under de-DE, including         │
     │   decimal.MaxValue and 28-digit fractions), so no RemoveTypeMap or      │
     │   custom write is needed for decimal. Registration is process-wide and  │
     │   runs once. Dapper then maps rows straight into the Reservation and    │
     │   SupplierStats records (SELECT column order must match the constructor │
     │   parameter order).                                                     │
     │ - Connection abstraction: IDbConnectionFactory.OpenConnectionAsync()    │
     │   returns a System.Data.Common.DbConnection. Repositories depend only   │
     │   on that and on IsolationLevel.Serializable for the write lock (SQLite │
     │   maps it to BEGIN IMMEDIATE). Only SqliteConnectionFactory references  │
     │   Microsoft.Data.Sqlite. The SQL text itself (ON CONFLICT, WITHOUT      │
     │   ROWID) is still SQLite-flavored.                                      │
     │ - The pure dedup decision is the static Reservation.Evaluate(existing,  │
     │   incoming) (Created, Duplicate, Stale, Updated), next to               │
     │   SameDetailsAs, so it is unit-testable without a DB. The repository    │
     │   only performs the write the status implies.                           │
     │ - IReservationRepository.UpsertAsync(reservation) runs in one write     │
     │   transaction:                                                          │
     │   a. SELECT the existing row by key.                                    │
     │   b. None: INSERT, giving Created.                                      │
     │   c. Identical: nothing is written, giving Duplicate.                   │
     │   d. Incoming updatedAtUtc is older: nothing is written, giving Stale.  │
     │   e. Otherwise UPDATE, giving Updated.                                  │
     │   f. For Created and Updated, increment SupplierStats.Ingested in the   │
     │      same transaction (atomic upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE  │
     │      SET Ingested = Ingested + 1).                                      │
     │ - ISupplierStatsRepository: IncrementThrottledAsync, GetAsync (zeros if │
     │   no row).                                                              │
     │ - Concurrency: the SELECT-then-write must not race (two identical       │
     │   concurrent requests must yield exactly one Created). Use an immediate │
     │   (write-locking) transaction. Confirm that Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's     │
     │   chosen isolation level really takes the write lock up front, and      │
     │   prove it with the concurrency test in Step 7. If it doesn't, fall     │
     │   back to a per-key SemaphoreSlim.                                      │
     │ - No explicit PRAGMA busy_timeout is needed: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite      │
     │   applies its Default Timeout (30s) as the busy timeout when a          │
     │   connection opens, so concurrent writers wait instead of throwing      │
     │   "database is locked".                                                 │
     │ - Unit tests (done, 84 total passing): DapperConfigurationTests proves  │
     │   the Dapper setup on a single in-memory connection with its own        │
     │   minimal table (date write format, nullable dates, price stored as     │
     │   text, record round trip incl. a Duplicate check, prices under de-DE,  │
     │   double registration harmless); it was verified to fail 11 of 12 when  │
     │   the RemoveTypeMap workaround is removed. Reservation.Evaluate (all    │
     │   outcomes, including equal updatedAtUtc and offset-insensitivity).     │
     │   DateTimeOffsetTypeHandler (UTC normalization, tick precision, culture │
     │   invariance with th-TH, round trip, chronological text sorting across  │
     │   offsets, malformed text and non-text values throw) and                │
     │   DecimalTypeHandler (read-only: exact parsing of stored text incl.     │
     │   extremes, culture invariance with de-DE, no float drift, malformed    │
     │   text and non-text values throw). SqliteConnectionFactory (rejects     │
     │   blank connection strings, returns a fresh open connection each time,  │
     │   fails cleanly on an unopenable database; uses Data Source=:memory: so │
     │   no file is needed). The repositories, initializer and real round      │
     │   trips need SQLite, so they are integration tests in Step 7.           │
     │ - Verified with a throwaway scratch test (deleted; recreate properly in │
     │   Step 7): text storage format, round trip, 20 parallel identical       │
     │   upserts give exactly 1 Created and 19 Duplicate with ingested == 1,   │
     │   10 parallel throttled increments give 10. With a weaker isolation     │
     │   level (ReadUncommitted, or earlier deferred: true) the concurrency    │
     │   test fails with SQLite Error 5: 'database is locked', so it genuinely │
     │   proves IsolationLevel.Serializable (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) is what makes    │
     │   it safe.                                                              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 4. Rate limiter (the interesting part)                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ - IRateLimiter.TryAcquire(id) -> RateLimitResult(Permitted,             │
     │   RetryAfter). (Step 4 done; the full suite is green.)                  │
     │ - Built beyond the original sketch: validation attributes on            │
     │   RateLimitOptions ([Range(1, int.MaxValue)] on the limit;              │
     │   [Range(typeof(TimeSpan), ...)] from one tick to a one-day sanity cap  │
     │   on the window) with ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart(), so a │
     │   bad config stops the app at startup (covered by                       │
     │   RateLimitingStartupValidationTests, which start a real host and fail  │
     │   if ValidateOnStart() is removed; also verified by real runs with      │
     │   PermitLimit=0 and Window=00:00:00; also verified culture-independent  │
     │   under de-DE, fr-FR, th-TH), AddRateLimiting() extension (binds the    │
     │   RateLimiting config section, TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System),    │
     │   singleton limiter), and RateLimiting defaults in appsettings.json.    │
     │ - The log stores monotonic TimeProvider.GetTimestamp() values           │
     │   (Queue<long>), not wall-clock DateTimeOffset, so clock adjustments    │
     │   cannot shorten or stretch the window. The clock is read inside the    │
     │   per-id lock so the queue stays chronological under contention. A      │
     │   request exactly one window old counts as expired.                     │
     │ - SlidingWindowRateLimiter implements the sliding window log algorithm  │
     │   (singleton): one log of accepted-request timestamps per id (the app   │
     │   uses the supplierId as the id). ConcurrentDictionary<string,          │
     │   WindowLog>, where each WindowLog holds a Queue<long> of monotonic     │
     │   timestamps (the log, in chronological order) guarded by a private     │
     │   _lock object.                                                         │
     │   - On each call (inside the lock): read the clock, then dequeue        │
     │     timestamps whose elapsed time is >= window. If count >= limit,      │
     │     reject with RetryAfter = window - elapsed(oldest), which is always  │
     │     strictly positive. Otherwise enqueue now and allow.                 │
     │   - Rejected calls enqueue nothing (per your decision).                 │
     │ - RateLimitOptions (limit = 100, window = 60s) bound via IOptions, so   │
     │   tests can use small values if needed.                                 │
     │ - Inject TimeProvider (built into .NET 8) instead of calling            │
     │   DateTime.UtcNow.                                                      │
     │ - Why a sliding log over a fixed window: the spec says "any rolling     │
     │   60-second window". A fixed window allows 200 requests across a        │
     │   boundary. Memory is bounded at 100 timestamps per supplier.           │
     │ - Known limitation (README): in-memory state is lost on restart and not │
     │   shared across instances. Idle windows are never evicted, which is     │
     │   fine at this scale.                                                   │
     │ - Unit tests (done; FakeTimeProvider, no DB). Verified by deliberately  │
     │   breaking the code: counting rejected requests, an off-by-one at the   │
     │   boundary, and removing the lock each turn the suite red.              │
     │   - 100 calls allowed, 101st rejected with a sensible RetryAfter.       │
     │   - After advancing 60s the supplier is allowed again, and the window   │
     │     is truly rolling (requests at t=0 and t=30 expire independently).   │
     │   - Boundary: a timestamp exactly 60s old has expired.                  │
     │   - Suppliers are isolated from each other.                             │
     │   - Rejected calls don't extend the window.                             │
     │   - Small custom RateLimitOptions are honored.                          │
     │   - Concurrency: 300 parallel calls produce exactly 100 allowed.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 5. Ingestion service (DONE)                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Built: Services/IReservationIngestionService,                           │
     │ ReservationIngestionService, IngestResult (a record with private        │
     │ constructor and two factories: Processed(status), which rejects         │
     │ Throttled, and Throttled(retryAfter); only the throttled outcome        │
     │ carries a RetryAfter), and a direct singleton registration in           │
     │ Program.cs (safe because it only depends on singletons; a one-line      │
     │ AddIngestion() wrapper was written and then removed as redundant).      │
     │ Shared hand-written fakes live in the test project's Fakes/ folder      │
     │ (FakeRateLimiter, FakeReservationRepository,                            │
     │ FakeSupplierStatsRepository, each able to record an ordered call log)   │
     │ for reuse by the Step 6 controller tests.                               │
     │ IReservationIngestionService.IngestAsync(Reservation) orchestrates:     │
     │ 1. limiter.TryAcquire(supplierId). If denied,                           │
     │    stats.IncrementThrottledAsync, then return Throttled(retryAfter).    │
     │ 2. Otherwise reservationRepo.UpsertAsync and return the outcome.        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ It returns a small result type (status plus optional RetryAfter), not   │
     │ exceptions. Exceptions are for exceptional cases only. Why this layer:  │
     │ the controller stays trivial and the logic is unit-testable with fakes. │
     │ - Unit tests (hand-written fake limiter and fake repositories):         │
     │   - Limiter allows, so the repository is called and its outcome is      │
     │     returned unchanged (Created, Updated, Duplicate, Stale).            │
     │   - Limiter denies, so the result is Throttled with the RetryAfter, the │
     │     throttled counter is incremented exactly once, and the repository   │
     │     is never called.                                                    │
     │   - The limiter is asked with the reservation's supplierId.             │
     │   - The cancellation token is passed through.                           │
     │   - A repository exception propagates (not swallowed).                  │
     │   - Also covered: call order (limiter before repository, and limiter    │
     │     then stats when throttled), a stats failure while throttling        │
     │     propagates and the repository is still not called, a null           │
     │     reservation is rejected before any collaborator is called,          │
     │     IngestResult rules, and two composition tests using the REAL        │
     │     SlidingWindowRateLimiter with a FakeTimeProvider (limit 3: exactly  │
     │     3 reach the repository, 2 are throttled and counted once each with  │
     │     RetryAfter equal to the window; a throttled supplier does not       │
     │     affect another and recovers after the window).                      │
     │   - Verified by deliberately breaking the service three ways, each      │
     │     turning the suite red: still writing when throttled, not counting a │
     │     throttled request, limiting by the wrong key (reservationId         │
     │     instead of supplierId).                                             │
     │   - Decisions to record in the README: (1) a stats-write failure while  │
     │     throttling propagates (500) instead of being swallowed, so a        │
     │     failing stats table also fails throttled requests; (2) a request    │
     │     that consumed a limiter slot still counts against the supplier even │
     │     if the later database write fails. Blank supplier ids never reach   │
     │     the limiter because request validation (Step 2) rejects them first; │
     │     the Step 6/7 tests must prove that ordering over HTTP.              │
     │   - More README notes from the Step 5 review: (3) a rejected request    │
     │     still costs one small counter write (the spec wants throttled       │
     │     requests counted), and SQLite has a single writer, so under a flood │
     │     throttled requests can queue on the write lock and a 429 could      │
     │     become a 500 after the busy timeout; the throttle protects the      │
     │     reservations table, not the database as a whole. (4) Supplier ids   │
     │     are case-sensitive ("Acme" and "acme" are different suppliers for   │
     │     the limiter, the table and the stats), which is consistent but a    │
     │     bypass vector. (5) Cancellation: a cancelled throttled-counter      │
     │     write is not counted, and a limiter slot consumed before a          │
     │     cancellation or failed write stays consumed.                        │
     │   - Step 5 review follow-ups done: the misleading "protects the         │
     │     database" comment was reworded, XML docs added (class, Throttled    │
     │     factory, interface <returns>), and tests added for cancellation     │
     │     propagation (repository and stats paths) and for Duplicate/Stale    │
     │     still consuming quota with the real limiter (verified to fail if    │
     │     quota were only counted for Created/Updated).                       │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Step 6. Controller and error handling (DONE)                            │

     │   until then). Incident during the revert: a trim of                    │
     │   ReservationRepository removed                                         │
     │   DapperConfiguration.RegisterTypeHandlers() from its constructor at    │
     │   the same moment it had been removed from AddDataAccess, so nothing    │
     │   registered the Dapper handlers: the real app stored dates in the      │

     │ - A real bug found while verifying, and fixed: the repository logging   │
     │   tests passed in the full suite but failed when run alone with "A      │
     │   parameterless default constructor ... is required for Reservation     │
     │   materialization". Cause: Dapper's type handlers are registered        │

     │   options, so enums are documented as strings); the text/plain string   │

     │   header (that would need an extra Swashbuckle package or a custom      │
     │   filter), and Throttled still appears in the status enum although a    │
     │   throttled request gets a 429 and never this body (the status          │
     │   description says so).                                                 │
     │ - Verified finding (offset-less timestamps): on a UTC+2 machine,        │
     │   "2026-07-01T10:15:00" (no offset) followed by the same instant        │
     │   written with Z returned Updated, not Duplicate: System.Text.Json      │
     │   reads an offset-less value as SERVER-LOCAL time. The spec's examples  │
     │   all carry Z, so this is an edge case.                                 │
     │   - DECISION (dropped for now): not validated, documented as a known    │
     │     limitation. A parse-time converter that rejected offset-less        │
     │     timestamps with a 400 (OffsetRequiredDateTimeOffsetConverter) was   │
     │     built, unit tested, mutation-checked and verified over real HTTP,   │
     │     then deliberately removed for scope: the spec's examples all carry  │
     │     Z and the field is named updatedAtUtc. It could not live in         │
     │     IngestReservationRequest.Validate() (nor in a custom validation     │
     │     attribute): the parsed DateTimeOffset of an offset-less value is    │
     │     identical to one written with the local offset, so the information  │
     │     is gone before any validation runs; a parse-time converter was the  │
     │     only reliable place. If revisited: reject with a 400 (strict,       │
     │     safest) or assume UTC (friendlier, but silently accepts ambiguity). │
     │   - README (Step 8), under assumptions/limitations: timestamps are      │
     │     expected to carry an explicit UTC offset (Z or +hh:mm), as in the   │
     │     assignment's examples. One without an offset is read as             │
     │     SERVER-LOCAL time by System.Text.Json, so a supplier that sends the │
     │     same instant in two styles (10:15:00 then 10:15:00Z) would get      │
     │     Updated instead of Duplicate on a server that does not run in UTC.  │
     │     With more time: reject offset-less timestamps with a 400 at parse   │
     │     time.                                                               │
     │ - POST /api/reservations/ingest maps the outcome:                       │

     │   - Decision: no SupplierStatsService. The controller injects           │
     │     ISupplierStatsRepository directly. The endpoint is a read-only      │
     │     query with no business logic, so a service would be a pass-through  │
     │     (one class, one interface, one fake, tests that only test the       │
     │     delegation). The POST has a service because it has real             │
     │     orchestration (throttle, then write); symmetry alone is not a       │
     │     reason for a shallow layer. If logic ever appears (derived values,  │
     │     caching, authorization), extract a service then; the repository     │
     │     interface makes that a small refactor. Cost to record in the        │

     │     and return 400 ProblemDetails for a blank one (the repository       │

     │     separate types by an earlier decision).                             │
     │ - GlobalExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, .NET 8) turns unexpected   │
     │   errors into a 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace leaked. Log the  │
     │   exception.                                                            │
     │   - Cancellation is not an error, and the framework already handles it  │
     │     (verified, so no special case in our handler): a scratch test with  │
     │     a real in-memory server cancelled the client request mid-flight.    │
     │     ASP.NET's exception middleware intercepted the                      │

     │     (no error log, no 500, handler not invoked) belongs in the Step 7   │
     │     integration tests.                                                  │
     │   - Consuming IngestResult without !: use if (result.RetryAfter is { }  │
     │     retryAfter) for the 429 branch (this also removes the nullable from │
     │     the happy path), then Created gives 201 and everything else 200.    │
     │     Put the whole-seconds, rounded-up Retry-After conversion in one     │
     │     small helper with unit tests (1ms gives 1, 60s gives 60, 60.0001s   │

     │ 7a. Integration test infrastructure (new, folder                        │

     │   which is acceptable.                                                  │
     │ - Direct database assertions through                                    │
     │   TempSqliteDatabase.ConnectionFactory plus Dapper (SELECT COUNT(*)     │
     │   FROM Reservations, the stored row, the SupplierStats row). This is    │

     │   code.                                                                 │

     │ 7b. The integration tests (about 14; each asserts the HTTP result AND   │
     │ the database)                                                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Dedup                                                                   │
     │ 1. Create: POST a new reservation, expect 201, body Created, no         │
     │    Location header, one row stored with the right values (price 450.10, │
     │    dates in UTC).                                                       │
     │ 2. Duplicate, proven by what did NOT happen: resend identical details   │

     │ 4. Stale: an older updatedAtUtc with different details, expect 200      │
     │    Stale, the row unchanged, Ingested unchanged.                        │
     │ 5. Composite identity: the same reservationId from two suppliers gives  │
     │    two independent rows, and updating one leaves the other untouched.   │

     │    Created and 19 Duplicate, one row, Ingested 1. This is what proves   │
     │    the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction works.                               │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Throttle                                                                │
     │ 7. The assignment's rule, with the real limit of 100: 101 requests from │
     │ one supplier (distinct reservation ids). The first 100 are not          │
     │ throttled, the 101st returns 429 application/problem+json with a        │
     │ Retry-After header, the reservations table holds 100 rows (the          │
     │ throttled request wrote nothing), and the stats read ingested 100,      │
     │ throttled 1.                                                            │
     │ 8. Isolation: while that supplier is throttled, another supplier's      │
     │ request still succeeds.                                                 │
     │ 9. The window clears, and Retry-After is rounded up (uses               │
     │ FakeTimeProvider and PermitLimit 2, no sleeping): throttled at t=0      │
     │ gives Retry-After: 60; after advancing 30.5 s it is 30; after advancing │
     │ to 59.9999 s it is 1 (never 0); after 60 s the supplier is accepted     │
     │ again.                                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Errors and the rest                                                     │

     │ is stored.                                                              │
     │ 11. Stats for an unknown supplier return {ingested: 0, throttled: 0}; a │

     │ 12. An unexpected failure returns a clean 500 (the one extra group you  │

※ recap: We're building the Mize reservations API with tests that prove dedup and throttling, and Step 7 (the test reset) is finished: 49 tests green, all seven mutation checks caught. Next, once you say go, is Step 8, the short README.

> can you list me the tests? go deep into the integration tests and explain     

  Searched for 1 pattern, ran 2 shell commands (ctrl+o to expand)

● The tests (49)

  How the integration tests work

  Every integration test builds its own ApiTest, which has three parts:
  - A fresh database. It is a temp SQLite file, created through
    TempSqliteDatabase.
  - The real app. ReservationsApiFactory starts the whole application in memory
    on that file. The real controllers, service, limiter, repositories and
    Dapper are all used. Only the clock (optionally) and the repository (in one
    test) can be swapped.
  - A way to read the database directly. ReservationsAsync() and StatsRowAsync()
    run SQL through Dapper. A test can therefore check what is actually stored,
    not only what the API says.

  Each test gets its own app because the rate limiter keeps its state in memory.
  A shared app would let one test's requests use up another test's quota.

  The first request in every test also proves that startup works: the schema is
  created, the Dapper type handlers are registered, and the connection string is
  read. That is why there are no separate tests for the initializer, type
  handlers or connection factory.

  Integration tests, 17 cases

  ReservationDedupTests (8 cases)

  1. ANewReservation_IsCreated_WithNoLocationHeader_AndStored
     - It POSTs a new reservation.
     - It expects a 201, no Location header, and the body {Created, acme, 
       res-1}.
     - It then reads the database. There is exactly one row, with the right room
       and price 450.10. Dates are stored as fixed UTC text
       (2026-08-01T00:00:00.0000000Z).
     - The stats row shows Ingested = 1.
     - This test also checks the date and decimal round trip through Dapper.
  2. AnIdenticalResend_IsADuplicate_AndNothingIsWritten (3 cases). Each case
     first creates res-1, snapshots the rows, then resends. It expects a 200
     Duplicate, rows equal to the snapshot, and Ingested still 1.
     - TheSameRequestAgain sends the same body.
     - ThePriceWrittenWithoutItsTrailingZero sends 450.1 instead of 450.10. That
       is the same price, so it must be a duplicate.
     - TheSameInstantsWrittenWithAnOffset sends the same moments as +02:00
       times. Dedup compares instants, not text, so it is still a duplicate.
     - The snapshot comparison is the proof that nothing was written.
  3. ChangedDetailsWithANewerUpdate_UpdateTheStoredReservation sends a new price
     with a newer updatedAtUtc. It expects a 200 Updated, still one row (an
     update replaces, it doesn't add), the new price and timestamp stored, and
     Ingested = 2.
  4. AnOlderUpdate_IsStale_AndTheStoredReservationIsLeftAlone sends a different
     price with an older updatedAtUtc. This simulates a delayed retry. It
     expects a 200 Stale, rows unchanged (the price 999 must not appear), and
     Ingested still 1.
  5. TheSameReservationIdFromTwoSuppliers_AreTwoIndependentReservations
     - acme/res-1 and globex/res-1 both return 201, so the second is not
       mistaken for a duplicate.
     - It then updates acme's reservation.
     - Globex's row must be byte-for-byte unchanged. This proves the composite
       key (supplierId, reservationId).
  6. TwentyIdenticalRequestsAtOnce_CreateExactlyOneReservation fires 20
     identical requests at once. It expects no 5xx, exactly 1 Created and 19
     Duplicate, one row, and Ingested = 1. It proves the BEGIN IMMEDIATE
     transaction. With a weaker isolation level, the mutation check showed this
     test fails.

  SupplierThrottleTests (3 cases)

  7. The101stRequestInAMinute_IsRejected_AndNothingIsWrittenForIt
     - It uses the real limit (100 per 60 s) and sends 101 requests from one
       supplier with distinct reservation ids.
     - The first 100 return 201 and the 101st returns 429
       application/problem+json with Retry-After: 60.
     - The table holds exactly 100 rows, and res-101 is not among them.
     - Stats read Ingested = 100, Throttled = 1.
     - It uses FakeTimeProvider and never advances it, so all 101 requests land
       in the same window and the test cannot be flaky.
  8. AnotherSupplier_IsNotAffected_WhileOneIsThrottled
     - The limit is set to 2. noisy sends 3 requests and the third gets a 429.
     - quiet then sends one request and gets a 201.
     - Stats are noisy 2 ingested and 1 throttled, quiet 1 ingested and 0
       throttled.
  9. WhenTheWindowClears_TheSupplierIsAcceptedAgain_AndRetryAfterIsRoundedUp
     - The limit is 2. After two accepted requests, the test makes one request
       at each point below and moves the fake clock between them.

  | Time      | Result                                         |
  |-----------|------------------------------------------------|
  | t=0       | 429, Retry-After: 60                           |
  | 30.5 s    | 429, Retry-After: 30 (29.5 s left, rounded up) |
  | 59.9999 s | 429, Retry-After: 1 (0.0001 s left, never 0)   |
  | 60 s      | 201                                            |

     - Stats end at Ingested = 3, Throttled = 3.
     - The 201 at 60 s shows that the 429s in between did not extend the window.

  ErrorHandlingTests (6 cases)

  10. InvalidInput_Returns400ProblemJson_AndStoresNothing (3 cases). The inputs
      are an empty object, checkOut == checkIn, and a negative price. Each must
      return a 400 application/problem+json, with no rows and no stats row.
      Invalid requests never reach the limiter or the database.
  11. Stats_ForASupplierThatNeverSentAnything_AreZero expects a 200 with
      {nobody, 0, 0}.
  12. Stats_WithABlankSupplierId_Returns400 calls the endpoint with %20 and
      expects a 400 application/problem+json.
  13. AnUnexpectedFailure_Returns500ProblemJson_WithNothingAboutTheFailureLeaked
      - It swaps in a repository that throws an exception with the message
        Server=prod-db;Password=hunter2.
      - It expects a 500 application/problem+json that contains traceId.
      - The body must not contain the message, the exception type name, or a
        stack trace.

  Unit tests, 32

  Domain/ReservationTests (12): the dedup rules
  - SameDetailsAs_IsFalse_WhenASingleDetailDiffers runs 5 cases, one each for
    room, check-in, check-out, price and updatedAtUtc.
  - SameDetailsAs_ComparesInstants_NotOffsets
  - SameDetailsAs_TreatsPricesWithDifferentScaleAsEqual
  - Evaluate_NothingStored_IsCreated
  - Evaluate_IdenticalDetails_IsDuplicate
  - Evaluate_DifferentDetailsWithNewerUpdate_IsUpdated
  - Evaluate_DifferentDetailsWithSameUpdatedAt_IsUpdated_NotStale
  - Evaluate_DifferentDetailsWithOlderUpdate_IsStale

  RateLimiting/SlidingWindowRateLimiterTests (6): the algorithm
  - First100Requests_ArePermitted_And101stIsRejected
  - ARequestExactlyOneWindowOld_HasExpired
  - Window_IsTrulyRolling_RequestsExpireIndependently
  - RejectedRequests_DoNotExtendTheWindow
  - Ids_AreIsolatedFromEachOther
  - ConcurrentRequests_NeverExceedTheLimit, which makes 300 parallel calls and
    expects exactly 100 permitted.

  Services/ReservationIngestionServiceTests (8): the orchestration, with fakes
  - WhenPermitted_TheRepositoryOutcomeIsReturnedUnchanged runs 4 cases (Created,
    Updated, Duplicate, Stale).
  - WhenThrottled_TheResultCarriesTheRetryAfter_AndTheThrottledCounterIsIncremen
    tedOnce
  - WhenThrottled_TheRepositoryIsNeverCalled
  - WithTheRealLimiter_DuplicateAndStaleRequestsStillConsumeQuota runs 2 cases.

  Contracts/IngestReservationRequestTests (6): validation and normalization
  - CheckOutEqualToCheckIn_FailsValidation
  - CheckOutBeforeCheckIn_FailsValidation
  - CheckOutThatLooksLaterOnTheClockButIsEarlierInTime_FailsValidation
  - NegativePrice_FailsValidation
  - ToReservation_TrimsIdentifiers
  - ToReservation_NormalizesTimestampsToUtc

  What the integration tests do not cover

  - Offset-less timestamps. That is a documented limitation.
  - A client aborting the request.
  - Logging levels, option validation and the Swagger output. I checked those by
    hand earlier.

  The unit tests overlap the integration tests on purpose in two places: the
  dedup rules (Evaluate) and the limiter algorithm. The unit tests pin down each
  rule precisely, and the integration tests show those rules working through
  real HTTP and SQLite.

> explain ApiTest                                                               

● ApiTest: one test's whole world

  ApiTest is a helper class. Each integration test creates one with using var 
  api = new ApiTest();, and it is disposed when the test ends. It bundles
  everything a test needs so the test body can read like a short story.

  What's inside

  Three pieces, built in the constructor:
  1. _database = new TempSqliteDatabase() creates a unique temp .db file path
     for this test.
  2. _factory = new ReservationsApiFactory(...) is the real application, pointed
     at that file. It is configured through the constructor arguments (see
     below).
  3. Client = _factory.CreateClient() is an HttpClient wired to the in-memory
     server. It runs no network code, but each request goes through the full
     ASP.NET pipeline (routing, validation, controller, exception handler).

  Creating the client is what starts the app, and startup is when
  DatabaseInitializer creates the schema in the fresh file. So by the time the
  constructor returns, the app is running and the tables exist.

  Optional constructor arguments change one thing about the app for a single
  test:
  - permitLimit overrides the throttle limit. Tests 8 and 9 set it to 2 so they
    don't need 100 requests.
  - timeProvider supplies a FakeTimeProvider, so the test controls the clock.
  - repository swaps the real repository for a fake. Only the clean-500 test
    does this, to make the repository throw.

  With no arguments you get the real app with the real limit of 100 per 60 s.

  Helpers for sending requests

  - PostAsync(body) POSTs JSON to /api/reservations/ingest.
  - GetStatsAsync(supplierId) calls the stats endpoint.
  - Body(...) builds a valid request body, with defaults for everything. A test
    overrides only what it cares about, for example Body("acme", "res-1", price:
    500m). Timestamps are plain strings so a test can choose the exact notation
    (Z versus +02:00).
  - ReadIngestAsync and ReadStatsAsync deserialize responses into small records.
    Those records use string Status, not the app's enum. The tests therefore
    check the actual JSON text, which also proves enums go out as strings.

  Helpers for looking at the database

  - ReservationsAsync() runs SELECT ... FROM Reservations through the same
    connection factory type the app uses, and returns every stored row.
    StoredReservation holds every column as text, exactly as stored. This is how
    tests assert things like CheckIn == "2026-08-01T00:00:00.0000000Z". It also
    lets a test compare "rows before" with "rows after" using plain equality,
    since records compare by value. That comparison is the proof that a
    duplicate or stale request wrote nothing.
  - StatsRowAsync(supplierId) reads the SupplierStats row. It returns null if
    the supplier has no row, which the invalid-input test uses to prove an
    invalid request left no trace.

  Cleanup

  Dispose() disposes the client, then the factory (which stops the app), then
  the database. Disposing the database clears SQLite's connection pool and
  deletes the .db, -wal, -shm and -journal files. The order matters: the pool
  must be cleared before the file can be deleted on Windows. That is why I found
  no leftover temp files.

  Why it is shaped this way

  - One per test, not shared. The limiter is an in-memory singleton, so a shared
    app would leak quota between tests. Starting about 17 apps costs only a few
    seconds in total.
  - Tests read the database themselves. A status code only tells you what the
    API claims. Reading the table tells you what actually happened.
  - The real wiring is under test. The test code never touches Dapper
    registration, the schema or DI. The app does all of that, so a mistake in it
    makes the first request of every test fail.

> dont you think this is too much for this assignment?                          

● Partly. I'd call the suite fine, with some overlap you could cut.

  What is proportionate
  - 49 tests, down from 201. The assignment asks for confidence in dedup and
    throttling, and the 17 integration cases map directly onto those two rules.
  - ApiTest plus the factory is about 150 lines. It's the price of tests that
    read like "POST this, expect that, check the table". Without it, every test
    would repeat that setup.
  - The 101-request test, the 20-parallel test and the window-clearing test are
    the strongest evidence in the repo. I'd keep all three.

  Where it's probably too much
  1. The service unit tests (8) mostly repeat integration tests 7 and 8.
     "Throttled never writes" and "the counter is incremented" are already
     proven against the real database. Only the "Duplicate and Stale still
     consume quota" cases add something the integration tests don't.
  2. The validation unit tests (6) partly overlap integration test 10. checkOut 
     == checkIn and the negative price are covered twice. The
     instant-versus-offset case and the trim and normalize tests are the only
     unique ones.
  3. The throttle fake-clock test checks tick-exact Retry-After values (60, 
     30, 1). That is precise, but it tests rounding, not the assignment's rule.
     A simpler version would just check that the supplier is accepted again
     after 60 s.
  4. Three variants of "duplicate" and three invalid-input cases could each be
     one.

  What I'd cut for a lighter version
  - Reduce the service unit tests to the 2 quota cases.
  - Reduce the validation unit tests to 2: the offset-instant case and the
    normalization case.
  - Merge the duplicate variants into one test and keep the rounding check.

  That brings it to roughly 35–38 tests with the same coverage of the two rules.
  The mutation table would still hold, because the integration tests catch all
  seven breaks.

  I'd keep the structure (integration-first, a small pure-logic unit suite) and
  trim the overlap if it feels heavy to you. A reviewer reading 49 focused tests
  won't penalize that, but they could see duplication as a lack of judgment. Do
  you want me to do the trim? I haven't changed anything.

  What unit-only can and can't prove

  Unit tests can prove:
  - The dedup decision rules (Reservation.Evaluate).
  - The limiter algorithm, including 300 parallel calls giving exactly 100
    permitted.
  - The service orchestration: throttle first, then write.
  - The validation rules.

  Unit tests can't prove, because the repository and database are faked or 
  absent:
  1. The dedup race. Two identical requests arriving together must produce one
     Created. That depends on the SQL transaction, not on Evaluate. This is the
     most realistic way for dedup to break.
  2. That a duplicate or stale request writes nothing. The decision is pure, but
     the write happens in the repository SQL.
  3. Plumbing that already failed once. The Dapper handlers were not registered,
     so the real app returned a 500 on the second POST while the build and all
     201 unit tests passed. Only running the real app caught it.
  4. The HTTP contract: 201 with no Location, 429 with Retry-After, and
     problem+json errors.

  My recommendation

  I'd go with C, or stay on A. I'd avoid B unless the assignment explicitly says
  not to write integration tests.

  - Not asking for something is different from ruling it out. "Enough tests to
    give us confidence" is outcome-based, and the dedup race is a reasonable
    thing for a reviewer to doubt.
  - B would let you honestly say "unit tests cover the logic". It would not let
    you say "I verified that duplicates don't write and that concurrent
    duplicates yield one Created". You would have to state that gap in the
    README.
  - C answers "does it actually work?" with 4 tests and keeps the infrastructure
    small.
